<!-- docs/rules/secret/server-env-in-client.md -->

# secret/server-env-in-client

Server env variable read in browser code.

A secret-named `process.env.X` or `import.meta.env.X` (API keys, tokens, passwords, database URLs) read in a module that ships to the browser.

- Default level: `warn`.
- Looks at: the project as a whole, across files.
- References: [CWE-200](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html).

## Why it matters

Only prefixed variables are copied into the browser bundle, so the value is undefined there. Renaming the variable with a public prefix "fixes" it by publishing the value, which is wrong for secrets.

## Flagged

`app/components/Chat.tsx` (warn):

```tsx
const key = process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY;
```

`app/components/Chat.tsx` (warn):

```tsx
const token = import.meta.env.GITHUB_TOKEN;
```

`lib/config.ts` (warn):

```ts
export const stripeKey = process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY;
```

## Not flagged

- `const key = process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY;` in `app/api/chat/route.ts`: route handlers run on the server
- `return Response.json({ ok: Boolean(key) });` in `app/api/chat/route.ts`: Boolean(key) });
- `const site = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL;` in `app/components/Chat.tsx`: public prefix
- `const mode = process.env.NODE_ENV;` in `app/components/Chat.tsx`: always defined
- `const build = process.env.CUSTOM_BUILD_ID;` in `app/components/Chat.tsx`: exposed through next.config env
- `const flag = process.env.FEATURE_FLAG;` in `app/page.tsx`: Server Component
- `export const apiBase = process.env.INTERNAL_API_URL;` in `lib/config.ts`: not a secret name; often a server-only flag in a shared module
- `DATABASE_URL: process.env.DATABASE_URL,` in `lib/env.ts`: createEnv keeps server variables on the server
- `clientSecret: process.env.FRAMER_CLIENT_SECRET as string,` in `lib/programs.ts`: nested in a shared config object

## How to fix

Read the variable in server code (a route handler, Server Action, or loader) and pass only the result to the browser.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore secret/server-env-in-client: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "secret/server-env-in-client": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/secret/server-env-in-client](../../../fixtures/rules/secret/server-env-in-client).

<!-- docs/rules/secret/in-prompt.md -->

# secret/in-prompt

Provider key in a prompt.

A provider key pasted into a prompt to the agent (Claude Code UserPromptSubmit, Cursor beforeSubmitPrompt, and the equivalents in other agents).

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: Set `prompts.secrets` to "warn" in ubon.json to warn instead of blocking.
- Looks at: agent actions in hooks: commands, file reads, and prompts.
- References: [CWE-200](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html).

## Why it matters

A prompt goes to the model provider and into the session transcript. Blocking it keeps the key out of both; a key that was sent cannot be recalled.

## How to fix

Put the key in an ignored .env file and refer to it by its variable name in the prompt.

## If the check is wrong

This check runs in agent hooks. Allow a command prefix with `commands.allow` in `ubon.json`, or set `"rules": { "secret/in-prompt": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

<!-- docs/rules/secret/in-tool-output.md -->

# secret/in-tool-output

Provider key in tool output.

Shell or tool output, returned to the agent, that contains a provider key.

- Default level: `warn`.
- Looks at: agent actions in hooks: commands, file reads, and prompts.
- References: [CWE-532](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/532.html).

## Why it matters

The output is now in the model context and the transcript. The agent should not repeat the key, and the user should know it was exposed.

## How to fix

Do not repeat the value. Tell the user which key appeared so they can decide whether to rotate it.

## If the check is wrong

This check runs in agent hooks. Allow a command prefix with `commands.allow` in `ubon.json`, or set `"rules": { "secret/in-tool-output": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

<!-- docs/rules/secret/read-sensitive-file.md -->

# secret/read-sensitive-file

Agent reads a secrets file.

The agent tries to read `.env*`, private keys, `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws/credentials`, `~/.npmrc`, or similar files through a read tool or a shell command such as `cat`.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: Returned as "ask" where the agent supports it, so a person approves the read; as "deny" elsewhere.
- Looks at: agent actions in hooks: commands, file reads, and prompts.
- References: [CWE-200](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html).

## Why it matters

Reading the file puts every secret in it into the model context and the transcript. A person should decide whether that is needed.

## How to fix

Ask the user for the variable names you need, or read `.env.example` instead.

## If the check is wrong

This check runs in agent hooks. Allow a command prefix with `commands.allow` in `ubon.json`, or set `"rules": { "secret/read-sensitive-file": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

<!-- docs/rules/web/sql-injection.md -->

# web/sql-injection

Request data in raw SQL.

Request data concatenated or interpolated into the SQL text of a raw query API: Prisma $queryRawUnsafe and $executeRawUnsafe, Drizzle sql.raw(), postgres.js sql.unsafe(), Knex raw(), pg and mysql2 query() and execute(), better-sqlite3 prepare() and exec(), Sequelize query() and literal().

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block when request data reaches the SQL text; warn when the value passed a schema whose constraints Ubon cannot read, and in example or template folders.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-89](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html), OWASP A05:2025.

## Why it matters

Whoever sends the request can rewrite the statement and read or change data the query was never meant to touch. Tagged templates such as Drizzle sql`...` and Prisma $queryRaw`...` send values separately from the SQL text, which is why they are safe.

## Flagged

`app/api/users/route.ts`:

```ts
const users = await prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(`SELECT * FROM "User" WHERE name = '${name}'`);
```

`app/api/users/route.ts`:

```ts
const sorted = await db.execute(sql.raw(`select * from users order by ${name}`));
```

`server/routes/items.js`:

```js
const sorted = await pool.query('SELECT * FROM items ORDER BY ' + req.query.sort);
```

`server/routes/items.js`:

```js
await pool.query(`INSERT INTO notes (title) VALUES ('${title}')`);
```

`server/search.ts`:

```ts
const stmt = db.prepare(`SELECT * FROM notes WHERE body LIKE '%${q}%'`);
```

`server/search.ts`:

```ts
const unsafe = await sql.unsafe(`select * from notes where title = '${q}'`);
```

`server/search.ts`:

```ts
const where = await qb('notes').whereRaw(`title = '${q}'`);
```

`server/trpc/posts.ts`:

```ts
return ctx.db.$queryRawUnsafe(`SELECT * FROM posts WHERE title ILIKE '%${input.term}%' LIMIT ${input.limit}`);
```

## Not flagged

- `const same = await prisma.$queryRaw'SELECT * FROM "User" WHERE name = ${name}';` in `app/api/users/route.ts`: Prisma tagged template sends name as a parameter
- `const rows = await db.execute(sql'select * from users where name = ${name}');` in `app/api/users/route.ts`: Drizzle sql tag parameterizes interpolated values
- `const found = await prisma.$executeRawUnsafe('UPDATE "User" SET verified = true WHERE email = $1', email);` in `app/api/users/route.ts`: the SQL text is constant; email is a positional parameter
- `const { rows } = await pool.query('SELECT * FROM items WHERE owner = $1', [req.query.owner]);` in `server/routes/items.js`: placeholder with a values array
- `const paged = await pool.query('SELECT * FROM items LIMIT 20 OFFSET ${(page - 1) * 20}');` in `server/routes/items.js`: numeric cast
- `const active = await pool.query('SELECT * FROM items WHERE status = '${STATUS}'');` in `server/routes/items.js`: module constant, not request data
- `const { rows } = await pool.query('SELECT * FROM items ORDER BY ${column}');` in `server/routes/items.js`: column checked against an allowlist first
- `const { rows } = await pool.query('SELECT * FROM items WHERE id IN (${placeholders})', ids);` in `server/routes/items.js`: placeholders only use the index
- `const hit = await cache.get('item:${req.params.id}');` in `server/routes/items.js`: a cache key, not SQL
- `const gql = await client.query({ query: ITEM_QUERY, variables: { id: req.params.id } });` in `server/routes/items.js`: GraphQL variables, not SQL text

## How to fix

Pass the value as a query parameter (a tagged sql`...` template, $queryRaw`...`, or a placeholder with a values array) instead of building the SQL string.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore web/sql-injection: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "web/sql-injection": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/web/sql-injection](../../../fixtures/rules/web/sql-injection).

<!-- docs/rules/web/command-injection.md -->

# web/command-injection

Request data in a shell command.

Request data in a command string run through a shell (child_process exec and execSync, spawn, execFile, or execa with shell: true, shelljs exec, sh -c), or used as the name of the program to run.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block when request data reaches the command; warn when the value passed a schema whose constraints Ubon cannot read, and in example or template folders.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html), OWASP A05:2025.

## Why it matters

A shell treats characters such as ; | $() and backticks as syntax, so whoever sends the request can append their own commands and run them with the permissions of the server process.

## Flagged

`app/api/convert/route.ts`:

```ts
await execAsync(`convert ${file} out.${format}`);
```

`app/api/convert/route.ts`:

```ts
spawn('convert', [file, 'out.png'], { shell: true });
```

`server/media.ts`:

```ts
await execa(`ffmpeg -i ${input} out.mp4`, { shell: true });
```

`server/media.ts`:

```ts
await execaCommand(`${input} --help`);
```

`server/tools.js`:

```js
const out = execSync('ping -c 1 ' + req.body.host);
```

`server/tools.js`:

```js
spawnSync('sh', ['-c', `git log ${req.body.ref}`]);
```

`server/tools.js`:

```js
const child = spawn(req.body.tool, ['--version']);
```

## Not flagged

- `execFile('convert', [file, 'out.${format}']);` in `app/api/convert/route.ts`: argument array without a shell
- `spawn('convert', [file, 'out.png']);` in `app/api/convert/route.ts`: fixed program, no shell
- `await execAsync('convert ${quote([file])} out.png');` in `app/api/convert/route.ts`: shell-quote escapes the value
- `await execAsync('convert input.png out.${Number(format)}');` in `app/api/convert/route.ts`: numeric cast
- `return Response.json({ ok: true });` in `app/api/convert/route.ts`: true });
- `await execa('ffmpeg', ['-i', input, 'out.mp4']);` in `server/media.ts`: execa without a shell passes input as one argument
- `await $'ffmpeg -i ${input} out.mp4';` in `server/media.ts`: zx quotes interpolated values
- `return c.json({ ok: true });` in `server/media.ts`: true });
- `res.send(execSync('git show ${ref}'));` in `server/tools.js`: ref must match an anchored character allowlist
- `db.exec('INSERT INTO jobs (name) VALUES ('${req.body.name}')');` in `server/tools.js`: a database client's exec, not a shell (see web/sql-injection)

## How to fix

Call execFile() or spawn() with a fixed program and the value as one element of the argument array, without shell: true.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore web/command-injection: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "web/command-injection": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/web/command-injection](../../../fixtures/rules/web/command-injection).

<!-- docs/rules/web/ssrf.md -->

# web/ssrf

Server request to a URL from the request.

Server-side fetch, axios, got, ky, undici, http.get, or page.goto whose URL (or host) comes from request data.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block when request data controls the scheme or host of the URL; warn when the data is appended directly to a base Ubon cannot read (it changes the host only if the base does not end with '/'), when the value passed a schema whose constraints Ubon cannot read, and in example or template folders. A fixed scheme and host with request data in the path or query is not reported.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-918](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/918.html), OWASP A01:2025.

## Why it matters

The server makes the request from inside your network, so whoever controls the URL can reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) and read the responses.

## Flagged

`app/api/favicon/route.ts` (warn):

```ts
const page = await fetch(`${config.upstream}${path}`);
```

`app/api/image/route.ts`:

```ts
return fetch(new URL(callback));
```

`app/api/preview/route.ts`:

```ts
const page = await fetch(url);
```

`server/proxy.js`:

```js
const { data } = await axios.get(req.query.url);
```

`server/proxy.js`:

```js
http.get(req.query.feed, (upstream) => upstream.pipe(res));
```

## Not flagged

- `const icon = await fetch('${FAVICONS}${domain}');` in `app/api/favicon/route.ts`: module constant fixes the host; the value goes in the query
- `const image = await fetch(parsed);` in `app/api/image/route.ts`: hostname checked against an allowlist
- `await fetch(target, { method: 'POST', body: '{}' });` in `app/api/image/route.ts`: validated by an allowlist helper
- `await fetch(icon);` in `app/api/image/route.ts`: hostname suffix check
- `const meta = await fetch('https://api.github.com/repos/${repo}');` in `app/api/preview/route.ts`: fixed scheme and host; request data only in the path
- `const self = await fetch(new URL('/api/health', request.url));` in `app/api/preview/route.ts`: same origin as the request
- `return fetch(target);` in `app/api/proxy/[...path]/route.ts`: the path and query go to a fixed upstream origin
- `fetch(params.get('u') ?? '/').then((r) => r.text()).then(setHtml);` in `components/LinkPreview.tsx`: the browser makes this request, not the server
- `const { data } = await axios.get('${API_BASE}/users/${req.params.id}');` in `server/proxy.js`: base URL from config; request data only in the path
- `const { data } = await axios.get('http://${host}/internal/status');` in `server/proxy.js`: the Host header names this server

## How to fix

Parse the URL with new URL() and check its hostname against an allowlist before fetching, or build the URL from a fixed base and pass the value only as a path segment or query parameter.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore web/ssrf: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "web/ssrf": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/web/ssrf](../../../fixtures/rules/web/ssrf).

<!-- docs/rules/web/path-traversal.md -->

# web/path-traversal

Request data in a file path.

fs reads, writes, and deletes, createReadStream, res.sendFile, res.download, Bun.file, and Bun.write with a path built from request data.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block when request data reaches the path; warn when the value passed a schema whose constraints Ubon cannot read, and in example or template folders.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-22](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html), OWASP A01:2025.

## Why it matters

A path segment such as ../../ or an absolute path lets whoever sends the request read or overwrite files outside the directory the code meant to use, such as .env files, keys, or source code.

## Flagged

`app/api/upload/route.ts`:

```ts
await writeFile(`public/uploads/${name}`, bytes);
```

`app/api/upload/route.ts`:

```ts
const css = await readFile(`themes/${theme}.css`, 'utf8');
```

`server/files.js`:

```js
res.sendFile(path.join(UPLOADS, req.params.name));
```

`server/files.js`:

```js
fs.readFile(`./uploads/${req.params.name}`, (err, data) => res.send(data));
```

`server/files.js`:

```js
await fs.promises.unlink(path.join(UPLOADS, req.params.name));
```

## Not flagged

- `await writeFile('public/uploads/${randomUUID()}.png', bytes);` in `app/api/upload/route.ts`: file name generated on the server
- `return Response.json({ ok: true });` in `app/api/upload/route.ts`: true });
- `const doc = await readFile('data/${id}.json', 'utf8');` in `app/api/upload/route.ts`: numeric cast
- `const page = await readFile('content/${slug}.md', 'utf8');` in `app/api/upload/route.ts`: rejects '..' and '/' first
- `return readFile(request.path);` in `lib/files.ts`: typed as FileRequest, not an HTTP request
- `res.sendFile(path.join(UPLOADS, path.basename(req.params.name)));` in `server/files.js`: basename keeps only the file name
- `res.sendFile(req.params.name, { root: UPLOADS });` in `server/files.js`: sendFile with a root rejects paths that leave it
- `fs.createReadStream(full).pipe(res);` in `server/files.js`: resolved path checked against the upload root
- `fs.createReadStream(target).pipe(res);` in `server/files.js`: path.relative check keeps the file inside the root
- `fs.readFile(path.join(__dirname, 'reports', 'summary.pdf'), (err, data) => res.send(data));` in `server/files.js`: constant path

## How to fix

Reduce the value to a file name with path.basename(), or resolve it with path.resolve(root, value) and reject it unless it starts with root plus path.sep.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore web/path-traversal: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "web/path-traversal": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/web/path-traversal](../../../fixtures/rules/web/path-traversal).

<!-- docs/rules/web/code-eval.md -->

# web/code-eval

Request data evaluated as code.

eval, new Function, vm.runIn*Context and vm.Script, setTimeout or setInterval with a string, dynamic import() or require(), and template compilers (lodash template, ejs, pug) with request data; eval, Function, and vm with any value that is not a constant.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block when request data reaches the code; warn for eval, Function, and vm with a value of unknown origin that is not a constant, when the value passed a schema whose constraints Ubon cannot read, and in example or template folders. Dynamic import() of unknown origin is not reported (code splitting uses it).
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-95](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/95.html), OWASP A05:2025.

## Why it matters

Evaluated strings run with every permission of the page or the server process, so request data there lets whoever sends it run their own code.

## Flagged

`lib/formula.ts` (warn):

```ts
return eval(formula);
```

`server/calc.js`:

```js
const result = eval(req.body.expression);
```

`server/calc.js`:

```js
const fn = new Function('x', req.body.body);
```

`server/calc.js`:

```js
const mod = await import(`./plugins/${req.query.name}.js`);
```

`server/calc.js`:

```js
setTimeout(req.body.code, 100);
```

`server/calc.js`:

```js
res.json(vm.runInNewContext(req.body.script, {}));
```

## Not flagged

- `return import('../locales/${locale}.json');` in `lib/formula.ts`: dynamic import of unknown origin is code splitting, not reported
- `return eval(text);` in `lib/formula.ts`: model output is reported by llm/output-to-sink, not here
- `setTimeout(() => res.end(), 100);` in `server/calc.js`: a function, not a string
- `const data = JSON.parse(req.body.payload);` in `server/calc.js`: parsing data does not run it
- `const globalObject = new Function('return this')();` in `server/calc.js`: constant code
- `const plugin = await load();` in `server/calc.js`: module chosen from a fixed map in code
- `define: eval('(${flags})'),` in `vite.config.ts`: build tool config files are not checked

## How to fix

Parse data instead of evaluating it (JSON.parse, a schema), and choose modules and templates from a fixed map in code.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore web/code-eval: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "web/code-eval": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/web/code-eval](../../../fixtures/rules/web/code-eval).

<!-- docs/rules/web/xss-html-sink.md -->

# web/xss-html-sink

Value rendered as HTML without sanitizing.

dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, Vue v-html, Svelte {@html}, or Astro set:html with request data (block) or with any value that is not a constant (warn).

- Default level: `warn`.
- Levels: block when request data reaches the HTML; warn for other values that are not constants, for unescaped JSON.stringify() output inside a <script> element, when the value passed a schema whose constraints Ubon cannot read, and in example or template folders. Constants, sanitizer output, escaped HTML (renderToString, code highlighters, QR code renderers), <style> content, and script bodies built in code are not reported. Model output at these sinks is reported by llm/output-to-sink.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-79](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/79.html), OWASP A05:2025.

## Why it matters

HTML sinks run any script or event handler inside the markup. When the markup can contain text from users, they can run code in the sessions of other users and act as them.

## Flagged

`app/providers.tsx` (warn):

```tsx
<script dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: `window.__USER__ = ${JSON.stringify(state.user)};` }} />
```

`app/search/page.tsx` (block):

```tsx
<h1 dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: `Results for ${q}` }} />
```

`components/Post.tsx` (warn):

```tsx
<div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }} />
```

`components/Post.tsx` (warn):

```tsx
<script type="application/ld+json" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: JSON.stringify(jsonLd) }} />
```

`src/app/search.component.ts` (block):

```ts
this.searchValue = this.sanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml(query);
```

`src/components/Comment.vue` (warn):

```vue
<div v-html="comment.body"></div>
```

`src/components/Comment.vue` (block):

```vue
<p v-html="note"></p>
```

`src/pages/notice.astro` (block):

```astro
<div set:html={message} />
```

## Not flagged

- `<script dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: THEME_SCRIPT }} />` in `app/layout.tsx`: constant theme-flash script
- `<script dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: ANALYTICS_SNIPPET }} />` in `app/layout.tsx`: constant imported from another module
- `<script dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: 'window.__STATE__ = ${serialized};' }} />` in `app/providers.tsx`: '<' escaped before it reaches the script
- `<script dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: themeScript(storageKey) }} />` in `app/providers.tsx`: script body built in code
- `<p>Results for {q}</p>` in `app/search/page.tsx`: JSX text is escaped
- `<div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }} />` in `components/CodeBlock.tsx`: state only ever set to highlighter output
- `<div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: preview }} />` in `components/CodeBlock.tsx`: set through .then(setPreview) from the highlighter
- `<div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: renderSVG(shareUrl) }} />` in `components/CodeBlock.tsx`: QR code SVG, the data is encoded as modules
- `<style dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: themeCss(code) }} />` in `components/CodeBlock.tsx`: CSS inside a <style> element
- `<div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: dark }} />` in `components/CodeBlock.tsx`: set from .then((html) => ...) on highlighter output

## How to fix

Render the value as text, or sanitize it with DOMPurify.sanitize() or sanitize-html before rendering it as HTML.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```

```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "web/xss-html-sink": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

<!-- docs/rules/web/webhook-unverified.md -->

# web/webhook-unverified

Webhook handler without signature verification.

A webhook handler that reads the request body and acts on it without verifying the provider signature (Stripe constructEvent, Svix or Standard Webhooks verify, @octokit/webhooks, an HMAC compared with timingSafeEqual).

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block when the handler writes state (database, ORM, Supabase, SQL, or a mutating fetch); warn when it only logs or calls helpers whose effect is unknown; warn in example, sample, and demo folders.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-345](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/345.html), [CWE-347](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html), OWASP A07:2025, OWASP A08:2025.

## Why it matters

Webhook URLs are public. Without a signature check anyone can post a fake "payment succeeded" or "user created" event and the handler will grant plans, credits, or accounts as if the provider sent it.

## Flagged

`app/api/stripe/route.ts` (block):

```ts
const body = await req.json();
```

`app/api/webhooks/resend/route.ts` (warn):

```ts
const event = await request.json();
```

`app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts` (block):

```ts
const body = await req.text();
```

`functions/src/index.ts` (block):

```ts
const event = req.body;
```

`server/index.js` (block):

```js
const { repository } = req.body;
```

`src/routes/webhooks.ts` (block):

```ts
const body = await c.req.json();
```

`supabase/functions/clerk-webhook/index.ts` (block):

```ts
const payload = await req.json();
```

`supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts` (block):

```ts
const event = await req.json();
```

## Not flagged

- `const body = await req.text();` in `app/api/billing/webhook/route.ts`: verified with constructEvent below
- `const { priceId } = await req.json();` in `app/api/checkout/route.ts`: a signed-in checkout route, not a receiver
- `const rawBody = await req.text();` in `app/api/hubspot/webhook/route.ts`: the signature is compared with a hash of the client secret and the body
- `const payload = await req.text();` in `app/api/webhooks/clerk/route.ts`: verified with svix below
- `const input = await req.json();` in `app/api/webhooks/configs/route.ts`: wrapped in an auth wrapper, a CRUD API for webhook settings
- `const job = await request.json();` in `app/api/webhooks/cron/route.ts`: shared secret checked above
- `const raw = await request.text();` in `app/api/webhooks/lemonsqueezy/route.ts`: HMAC compared with timingSafeEqual below
- `const body = await req.json();` in `app/api/webhooks/qstash/route.ts`: QStash signature verified by the wrapper
- `return Response.json({ ok: true });` in `app/api/webhooks/resend/route.ts`: true });
- `const body = await req.json();` in `app/api/webhooks/settings/route.ts`: authenticated settings endpoint

## How to fix

Verify the provider's signature on the raw body before acting on the event.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore web/webhook-unverified: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "web/webhook-unverified": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/web/webhook-unverified](../../../fixtures/rules/web/webhook-unverified).

<!-- docs/rules/web/weak-token-randomness.md -->

# web/weak-token-randomness

Credential generated with Math.random().

Math.random() used to produce a token, session ID, password, one-time code, invite code, API key, nonce, salt, or secret.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block; warn for a bare token, session ID, or nonce outside server code, request handlers, and auth files or functions (markers, CLI session names, chat IDs, temp file names), and in example, sample, and demo folders.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-330](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/330.html), [CWE-338](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/338.html), OWASP A04:2025.

## Why it matters

Math.random() is not a cryptographic generator: its output can be predicted from earlier values, so tokens built from it can be guessed. Password reset tokens, session IDs, and one-time codes built this way let an attacker take over accounts.

## Flagged

`app/api/otp/route.ts`:

```ts
const otp = Math.floor(100000 + Math.random() * 900000).toString();
```

`app/api/otp/route.ts`:

```ts
const code = Math.floor(1000 + Math.random() * 9000);
```

`examples/magic-link/server.ts` (warn):

```ts
const token = Math.random().toString(36).slice(2);
```

`lib/accounts.ts`:

```ts
return db.user.create({ data: { email, password: makeRandomString(12) } });
```

`lib/auth/tokens.ts`:

```ts
const resetToken = Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 15);
```

`lib/auth/tokens.ts`:

```ts
result += chars.charAt(Math.floor(Math.random() * chars.length));
```

`lib/auth/tokens.ts`:

```ts
const inviteCode = randomString(8).toUpperCase();
```

`lib/cli-session.ts` (warn):

```ts
const rand = Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 6);
```

## Not flagged

- `if (Math.random() < 0.1) console.info('sampled request');` in `app/api/otp/route.ts`: sampling
- `return Response.json({ ok: true });` in `app/api/otp/route.ts`: true });
- `const [width] = useState(() => '${Math.floor(Math.random() * 40) + 50}%');` in `components/ChatList.tsx`: skeleton width for the UI
- `const color = COLORS[Math.floor(Math.random() * COLORS.length)];` in `components/ChatList.tsx`: picking an item from a list
- `const maxTokens = Math.floor(Math.random() * 500) + 100;` in `components/ChatList.tsx`: a token count, not a credential
- `const showPasswordHint = Math.random() > 0.5;` in `components/ChatList.tsx`: a comparison is sampling, not generation
- `const messages = items.map((text) => ({ id: generateUUID(), text }));` in `components/ChatList.tsx`: message IDs are not credentials
- `<li key={Math.random()}>{m.text}</li>` in `components/ChatList.tsx`: list keys are not credentials */}</li>
- `password: makeRandomString(5),` in `lib/accounts.ts`: sample users built by a function named as fake data
- `const token = sampleTokens[Math.floor(Math.random() * sampleTokens.length)];` in `lib/ai/simulate-stream.ts`: picks a word for a simulated model stream

## How to fix

Generate the value with crypto.randomBytes() or crypto.randomUUID() in Node, or crypto.getRandomValues() in the browser.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore web/weak-token-randomness: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "web/weak-token-randomness": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/web/weak-token-randomness](../../../fixtures/rules/web/weak-token-randomness).

<!-- docs/rules/web/cors-credentials-wildcard.md -->

# web/cors-credentials-wildcard

CORS allows any origin with credentials.

Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to * or to the request's own Origin while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is true, in header objects, header calls, the cors package, Hono, Fastify, Koa, NestJS, Next.js headers(), vercel.json, or netlify.toml.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block for an origin copied from the request, origin: true, or an origin callback that accepts every origin, with credentials (and for * in @koa/cors, which echoes the Origin header); warn for a literal * with credentials, which browsers refuse, and in example, sample, and demo folders.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-942](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/942.html), [CWE-346](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/346.html), OWASP A01:2025, OWASP A02:2025.

## Why it matters

With credentials allowed, a reflected origin lets any website make requests with the user's cookies and read the responses, which exposes account data to every page the user visits. Browsers refuse a literal * with credentials, so that setting breaks credentialed requests instead of exposing data, and the usual workaround of echoing the Origin header opens the hole.

## Flagged

`server.js` (block):

```js
app.use('/v1', cors({ origin: true, credentials: true }));
```

`server.js` (warn):

```js
app.use('/v2', cors({ origin: '*', credentials: true }));
```

`server.js` (warn):

```js
app.use('/v3', cors({ credentials: true }));
```

`server.js` (block):

```js
app.use('/v4', cors({ origin: (origin, callback) => callback(null, true), credentials: true }));
```

`server.js` (block):

```js
res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', req.headers.origin);
```

`server.js` (block):

```js
res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', req.headers.origin || '*');
```

`server.js` (warn):

```js
res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', '*');
```

`src/index.ts` (block):

```ts
app.use('/api/*', cors({ origin: (origin) => origin, credentials: true }));
```

## Not flagged

- `app.use('/v5', cors({ origin: ALLOWED_ORIGINS, credentials: true }));` in `server.js`: fixed list of origins
- `app.use('/v6', cors({ origin: (origin, cb) => cb(null, ALLOWED_ORIGINS.includes(origin)), credentials: true }));` in `server.js`: the callback checks a list
- `app.use('/public', cors());` in `server.js`: public API without credentials
- `app.use('/assets', cors({ origin: '*' }));` in `server.js`: wildcard without credentials
- `app.use('/config', cors({ origin: process.env.CORS_ORIGIN, credentials: true }));` in `server.js`: origin from configuration
- `res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', origin);` in `server.js`: checked against a list before echoing
- `res.header('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', '*');` in `server.js`: no credentials header
- `module.exports = cors({ origin: true, credentials: true });` in `tests/cors.test.js`: test code
- `app.use('/public/*', cors());` in `src/index.ts`: public routes without credentials
- `app.use('/app/*', cors({ origin: (origin) => (origin.endsWith('.example.com') ? origin : null), credentials: true }));` in `src/index.ts`: the callback checks the domain

## How to fix

Allow only a fixed list of trusted origins when credentials are enabled.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore web/cors-credentials-wildcard: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "web/cors-credentials-wildcard": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/web/cors-credentials-wildcard](../../../fixtures/rules/web/cors-credentials-wildcard).

<!-- docs/rules/web/jwt-unverified.md -->

# web/jwt-unverified

JWT claims used without verifying the signature.

Access decisions based on jwt.decode(), decodeJwt(), or jwtDecode() output with no verify call on the same token, JWT options that accept the none algorithm, and ignoreExpiration: true.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block when a claim decides access (a branch, a database lookup, the request user, or the return value of an auth helper); warn for display-only decodes, checks of time claims alone, tokens from a network response, and code in example, sample, and demo folders.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-347](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/347.html), [CWE-345](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/345.html), OWASP A07:2025, OWASP A04:2025.

## Why it matters

Decoding a JWT only base64-decodes it; anyone can write a token with any user ID or role. Without a signature check, the server trusts whatever the client sends, and accepting alg none or expired tokens has the same effect.

## Flagged

`app/api/me/route.ts` (block):

```ts
const { payload } = decode(token);
```

`app/api/oauth/callback/route.ts` (warn):

```ts
const profile = jwt.decode(tokens.id_token) as { email: string };
```

`app/api/profile/route.ts` (block):

```ts
const decoded = jwt.decode(token) as { userId: string } | null;
```

`app/api/profile/route.ts` (warn):

```ts
const claims = jwt.decode(token);
```

`lib/auth.ts` (block):

```ts
const { sub, email } = jwt.decode(token) as JwtPayload;
```

`lib/auth.ts` (warn):

```ts
const { exp } = jwt.decode(token) as JwtPayload;
```

`middleware.ts` (block):

```ts
const payload = decodeJwt(token);
```

`server/app.js` (block):

```js
req.user = jwt.decode(token);
```

## Not flagged

- `const decoded = jwt.decode(token) as { sub: string };` in `__tests__/auth.test.ts`: tests inspect tokens directly
- `const { name, role } = jwtDecode<{ name: string; role: string }>(token);` in `components/UserBadge.tsx`: browser code; the server verifies the token
- `const header = jwt.decode(token, { complete: true })?.header;` in `lib/auth.ts`: reads the key ID, then verifies below
- `return jwt.verify(token, key, { algorithms: ['RS256'] });` in `lib/auth.ts`: fixed algorithms list
- `const { exp } = jwt.decode(token) as JwtPayload;` in `lib/auth.ts`: our own token, signed on the line above
- `const decoded = jwt.decode(token) as { id?: string } | null;` in `lib/auth.ts`: called from verifyToken, which verifies with the owner's key
- `{ secretOrKey: process.env.JWT_SECRET, algorithms: ['HS256'], ignoreExpiration: false },` in `server/app.js`: fixed algorithm and expiry enforced

## How to fix

Verify the token with jwt.verify() or jwtVerify() (with a fixed algorithms list) before trusting any claim.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore web/jwt-unverified: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "web/jwt-unverified": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/web/jwt-unverified](../../../fixtures/rules/web/jwt-unverified).

<!-- docs/rules/web/open-redirect.md -->

# web/open-redirect

Redirect to a URL from the request.

redirect() (Next.js, Remix, React Router, SvelteKit), NextResponse.redirect, Response.redirect, res.redirect, c.redirect, a Location header, router.push or router.replace, or location.href with a target from request data and no same-origin check.

- Default level: `warn`.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-601](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/601.html), OWASP A01:2025.

## Why it matters

A link to your site that forwards to a look-alike site borrows the trust people have in your domain, which makes phishing pages and stolen OAuth codes look legitimate.

## Flagged

`app/api/auth/callback/route.ts`:

```ts
return NextResponse.redirect(new URL(next, request.url));
```

`app/auth/confirm/route.ts`:

```ts
if (next) return NextResponse.redirect(requestUrl.origin + next);
```

`app/login/actions.ts`:

```ts
redirect(destination);
```

`components/AfterLogin.tsx`:

```tsx
router.push(params.get('callbackUrl') ?? '/');
```

`components/AfterLogin.tsx`:

```tsx
window.location.href = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('next') ?? '/';
```

`server/auth.js`:

```js
res.redirect(req.query.returnTo);
```

## Not flagged

- `if (searchParams.has('error')) return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/login', request.url));` in `app/api/auth/callback/route.ts`: constant path on the request's own origin
- `return NextResponse.redirect(new URL(target, request.url));` in `app/api/auth/callback/route.ts`: only relative paths pass the check
- `return NextResponse.redirect(url);` in `app/api/auth/callback/route.ts`: origin compared with the request's origin
- `return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/${workspace}/links?created=${requestUrl.searchParams.get('link')}', request.url));` in `app/auth/confirm/route.ts`: the value is in the query after a fixed path
- `redirect('/login?next=${encodeURIComponent(pathname)}');` in `app/login/actions.ts`: fixed path; the value is only in the query
- `router.replace('/onboarding?step=${params.get('step')}');` in `components/AfterLogin.tsx`: fixed path
- `<button type="button" onClick={() => router.push('/${slug}/settings')}>` in `components/WorkspaceNav.tsx`: a route parameter as one path segment
- `res.redirect(302, '/users/${req.params.id}');` in `server/auth.js`: fixed first path segment
- `res.redirect(next);` in `server/auth.js`: checked against an allowlist

## How to fix

Accept only relative paths (target.startsWith('/') && !target.startsWith('//')), or compare new URL(target, base).origin with your own origin before redirecting.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore web/open-redirect: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "web/open-redirect": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/web/open-redirect](../../../fixtures/rules/web/open-redirect).

<!-- docs/rules/web/insecure-cookie.md -->

# web/insecure-cookie

Session cookie without httpOnly or secure.

A cookie named like a session or token (session, sid, token, auth, jwt, access_token, refresh_token, remember) set without httpOnly or without secure, or set from browser JavaScript.

- Default level: `warn`.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-1004](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1004.html), [CWE-614](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/614.html), OWASP A07:2025.

## Why it matters

Without httpOnly, any script on the page (an XSS bug, a compromised dependency) can read the session cookie and use it elsewhere. Without secure, the browser also sends it over plain HTTP, where it can be intercepted.

## Flagged

`server.js`:

```js
res.cookie('token', token);
```

`server.js`:

```js
res.cookie('remember_me', '1', { maxAge: 30 * 24 * 3600 * 1000, httpOnly: true });
```

`server.js`:

```js
res.setHeader('Set-Cookie', `session=${token}; Path=/; SameSite=Lax`);
```

`server.js`:

```js
res.cookie(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME, sign(req.body), { httpOnly: true });
```

`src/index.ts`:

```ts
setCookie(c, 'auth', token, { path: '/' });
```

`app/api/login/route.ts`:

```ts
cookieStore.set('session', token);
```

`app/api/login/route.ts`:

```ts
(await cookies()).set({ name: 'refresh_token', value: token, httpOnly: true });
```

`app/api/login/route.ts`:

```ts
res.cookies.set('access_token', token, { secure: true });
```

## Not flagged

- `res.cookie('connect.sid', token, { httpOnly: true, secure: true });` in `server.js`: both flags
- `res.cookie('XSRF-TOKEN', req.csrfToken());` in `server.js`: CSRF cookies must be readable by scripts
- `res.cookie('locale', 'en');` in `server.js`: not an auth cookie
- `res.setHeader('Set-Cookie', ['session=${token}; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure']);` in `server.js`: both flags in the string
- `res.setHeader('Set-Cookie', 'jwt=${token}; Path=/; HttpOnly${process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? '; Secure' : ''}');` in `server.js`: Secure is added in production
- `res.json({ ok: true });` in `server.js`: true });
- `res.cookie(THEME_COOKIE_NAME, 'dark');` in `server.js`: a constant named after a non-auth cookie
- `setCookie(c, 'auth', token, { path: '/', httpOnly: true, secure: true });` in `src/index.ts`: both flags
- `setCookie(c, 'auth', token, { httpOnly: true, prefix: 'secure' });` in `src/index.ts`: the __Secure- prefix makes it secure
- `setCookie(c, 'color_mode', 'dark');` in `src/index.ts`: not an auth cookie

## How to fix

Set the cookie with httpOnly: true and secure: true (secure may depend on NODE_ENV for local development).

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore web/insecure-cookie: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "web/insecure-cookie": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/web/insecure-cookie](../../../fixtures/rules/web/insecure-cookie).

<!-- docs/rules/web/token-in-web-storage.md -->

# web/token-in-web-storage

Auth token in localStorage or sessionStorage.

localStorage or sessionStorage used to store a value named like an auth credential (token, accessToken, refreshToken, jwt, session, apiKey, password).

- Default level: `warn`.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-922](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/922.html), OWASP A07:2025.

## Why it matters

Every script on the page can read web storage, so one XSS bug or compromised dependency is enough to steal the token and use it elsewhere. An httpOnly cookie keeps the token out of reach of scripts.

## Flagged

`src/components/Settings.tsx`:

```tsx
const [apiKey, setApiKey] = useLocalStorage('openai-api-key', '');
```

`src/lib/auth.ts`:

```ts
localStorage.setItem('token', data.token);
```

`src/lib/auth.ts`:

```ts
localStorage.setItem('accessToken', data.access_token);
```

`src/lib/auth.ts`:

```ts
sessionStorage.setItem(TOKEN_KEY, data.token);
```

`src/lib/auth.ts`:

```ts
localStorage.setItem('user', JSON.stringify({ ...data.user, jwt: data.jwt }));
```

`src/lib/auth.ts`:

```ts
window.localStorage.refresh_token = tokens.refresh_token;
```

## Not flagged

- `localStorage.setItem('token', 'test-token');` in `src/__tests__/auth.test.ts`: tests set up storage directly
- `const [draft, setDraft] = useLocalStorage('chat-input', '');` in `src/components/Settings.tsx`: a draft message
- `localStorage.setItem('theme', theme);` in `src/components/Settings.tsx`: theme preference
- `localStorage.setItem('locale', locale);` in `src/components/Settings.tsx`: language preference
- `localStorage.setItem('sidebar:state', String(open));` in `src/components/Settings.tsx`: UI state
- `localStorage.setItem('chat-session', JSON.stringify(messages));` in `src/components/Settings.tsx`: a chat transcript, not an auth session
- `localStorage.setItem('maxTokens', String(maxTokens));` in `src/components/Settings.tsx`: a model token limit
- `sessionStorage.setItem('hasSeenOnboarding', 'true');` in `src/components/Settings.tsx`: a flag
- `localStorage.setItem('tokenExpiresAt', String(data.expiresAt));` in `src/lib/auth.ts`: an expiry time, not the token
- `localStorage.removeItem('token');` in `src/lib/auth.ts`: removing is what logout should do

## How to fix

Keep the session in an httpOnly, secure cookie set by the server, or hold the token in memory only.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore web/token-in-web-storage: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "web/token-in-web-storage": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/web/token-in-web-storage](../../../fixtures/rules/web/token-in-web-storage).

<!-- docs/rules/data/rls-disabled.md -->

# data/rls-disabled

Supabase table without row level security.

A table in a schema exposed by the Supabase Data API (public, plus the schemas in supabase/config.toml) that no migration or declarative schema gives row level security, or whose row level security is disabled.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block for tables; warn for views created without security_invoker, materialized views, and partitions (which do not inherit row level security from their parent); warn for everything under example and template folders. Tables whose privileges are revoked from both anon and authenticated are not reported.
- Looks at: the project as a whole, across files.
- References: [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html), [CWE-862](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/862.html), OWASP A01:2025.

## Why it matters

Supabase grants the anon and authenticated roles access to tables in exposed schemas. Without row level security, anyone with the project URL and the anon key, which ships in every client bundle, can read and change every row.

## Flagged

`supabase/migrations/20240501000000_add_invoices.sql` (block):

```sql
create table public.invoices (
```

`supabase/migrations/20240301000000_tables.sql` (block):

```sql
create table public.comments (id uuid primary key, body text);
```

`supabase/migrations/20240301000000_tables.sql` (block):

```sql
create table public.labels (id int, name text);
```

`supabase/migrations/20240101000000_init.sql` (block):

```sql
create table todos (
```

`supabase/migrations/20240101000000_init.sql` (block):

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "public"."Audit Log" (
```

`supabase/migrations/20240101000000_init.sql` (block):

```sql
create table api.orders (
```

`supabase/migrations/20240201000000_changes.sql` (block):

```sql
alter table public.flags disable row level security;
```

`supabase/migrations/20240201000000_changes.sql` (block):

```sql
create table archive as select * from todos;
```

## Not flagged

- `create table public.legacy_logs (id bigserial primary key, line text);` in `supabase/migrations/20240101000000_init.sql`: existing debt in an unchanged migration is not reported in diff mode
- `create table public.invoice_lines (` in `supabase/migrations/20240501000000_add_invoices.sql`: row level security enabled in the same migration
- `create table public.projects (id uuid primary key, owner uuid);` in `supabase/migrations/20240301000000_tables.sql`: the DO block below enables row level security on every public table
- `create table public.tasks (id uuid primary key, project uuid);` in `supabase/migrations/20240301000000_tables.sql`: the DO block below enables row level security on every public table
- `create table public.tags (id int);` in `supabase/migrations/20240301000000_tables.sql`: the EXECUTE string below enables it
- `create table public.profiles (` in `supabase/migrations/20240101000000_init.sql`: row level security is enabled right below
- `create table private.api_keys (` in `supabase/migrations/20240101000000_init.sql`: the private schema is not exposed through the Data API
- `create temporary table import_scratch (line text);` in `supabase/migrations/20240101000000_init.sql`: temporary tables are not exposed
- `create table public.teams (` in `supabase/migrations/20240101000000_init.sql`: a later migration enables row level security
- `create table staging_items (id int);` in `supabase/migrations/20240101000000_init.sql`: renamed below, and the new name gets row level security

## How to fix

Enable row level security on the table in the same migration (`alter table <name> enable row level security;`) and add policies for the access each role needs.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```

```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "data/rls-disabled": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

<!-- docs/rules/data/permissive-policy.md -->

# data/permissive-policy

Supabase policy that allows every row.

A `create policy` for insert, update, delete, or all whose `using` or `with check` expression is `true` (or, on storage.objects, only a bucket filter) for anon, authenticated, or public. A select policy with `using (true)` is a warning.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block for insert, update, delete, and all policies; warn for select policies (often meant for public content), for update policies whose using clause restricts rows but whose with check is true, and for everything under example and template folders. Restrictive policies and policies only for service_role or other roles are ignored.
- Looks at: the project as a whole, across files.
- References: [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html), [CWE-862](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/862.html), OWASP A01:2025.

## Why it matters

A policy whose check is `true` turns row level security off for the roles it names. Sign-up is open on most Supabase projects, so "authenticated" means anyone who creates an account, and "anon" or "public" means anyone with the anon key.

## Flagged

`supabase/migrations/20240601000000_message_edits.sql` (block):

```sql
create policy "Anyone can edit messages" on public.messages for update using (true) with check (true);
```

`supabase/migrations/20240101000000_posts.sql` (warn):

```sql
create policy "Anyone can read posts" on public.posts for select using (true);
```

`supabase/migrations/20240101000000_posts.sql` (block):

```sql
create policy "Anyone can create posts" on public.posts for insert with check (true);
```

`supabase/migrations/20240101000000_posts.sql` (block):

```sql
create policy "Signed-in users can edit posts" on public.posts
```

`supabase/migrations/20240101000000_posts.sql` (block):

```sql
create policy "Logged-in users can delete" on public.posts
```

`supabase/migrations/20240101000000_posts.sql` (warn):

```sql
create policy "Users update own notes" on public.notes
```

`supabase/migrations/20240201000000_storage_and_changes.sql` (block):

```sql
create policy "Avatar uploads" on storage.objects for insert to authenticated with check (bucket_id = 'avatars');
```

`supabase/migrations/20240201000000_storage_and_changes.sql` (warn):

```sql
create policy "Avatars are public" on storage.objects for select using (bucket_id = 'avatars');
```

## Not flagged

- `create policy "Anyone can post" on public.messages for insert with check (true);` in `supabase/migrations/20240101000000_init.sql`: existing policy in an unchanged migration is not reported in diff mode
- `create policy "Senders can delete their messages" on public.messages for delete to authenticated using (sender = (select auth.uid()));` in `supabase/migrations/20240601000000_message_edits.sql`: checks the sender
- `create policy "Owners can edit their posts" on public.posts` in `supabase/migrations/20240101000000_posts.sql`: checks the row owner
- `create policy "Owners can delete their posts" on public.posts for delete using (auth.uid() = user_id);` in `supabase/migrations/20240101000000_posts.sql`: checks the row owner
- `create policy "Service role manages posts" on public.posts for all to service_role using (true) with check (true);` in `supabase/migrations/20240101000000_posts.sql`: only the service_role, which bypasses row level security anyway
- `create policy "Hide flagged posts" on public.posts as restrictive for select to authenticated using (true);` in `supabase/migrations/20240101000000_posts.sql`: restrictive policies only narrow access
- `create policy "Temporary open access" on public.posts for all using (true);` in `supabase/migrations/20240101000000_posts.sql`: dropped in a later migration
- `create policy "Private log writes" on private.audit for insert with check (true);` in `supabase/migrations/20240101000000_posts.sql`: the private schema is not exposed through the Data API
- `create policy "Own avatar uploads" on storage.objects for insert to authenticated with check (` in `supabase/migrations/20240201000000_storage_and_changes.sql`: the folder must match the user id
- `create policy "Editors update docs" on public.docs for update using (public.is_editor(team_id));` in `supabase/migrations/20240201000000_storage_and_changes.sql`: the alter below replaces this check

## How to fix

Replace `true` with a check on the row owner, such as `(select auth.uid()) = user_id`, or limit the policy to service_role.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore data/permissive-policy: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "data/permissive-policy": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).
