<!-- docs/rules/data/service-role-in-client.md -->

# data/service-role-in-client

Supabase service role key in browser code.

A Supabase client created with the service role or secret key (SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY, an sb_secret_ key, or a JWT with role service_role) in a module that ships to the browser.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block when the client is created at module level, in a 'use client' module, in a single-page app, or inside a function that browser code calls; warn when it is created inside a function of a shared module that browser code imports but does not call, and under example and template folders.
- Looks at: the project as a whole, across files.
- References: [CWE-798](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html), [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html), OWASP A01:2025.

## Why it matters

The service role key bypasses row level security and can read, change, and delete every row. Browser code is public: the key either ships in the bundle, or it is undefined there and the usual next step, renaming it with a public prefix, publishes it.

## Flagged

`app/admin/page.tsx` (block):

```tsx
const admin = createClient(supabaseUrl, process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY!);
```

`app/admin/page.tsx` (block):

```tsx
const client = createClient(supabaseUrl, serviceKey);
```

`lib/supabase-admin.ts` (block):

```ts
export const adminClient = createClient(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!, serviceRole!, {
```

`lib/supabase.ts` (warn):

```ts
return createSupabaseClient(url, process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY!);
```

`src/lib/supabase.ts` (block):

```ts
export const admin = createClient(url, serviceRoleKey);
```

`src/lib/supabase.ts` (block):

```ts
export const legacy = new SupabaseClient(url, 'sb_secret_...UT6j');
```

## Not flagged

- `const admin = createClient(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!, process.env.SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY!);` in `app/admin/actions.ts`: a Server Action module stays on the server
- `const anon = createClient(supabaseUrl, 'eyJhbGciOiJI...');` in `app/admin/page.tsx`: the anon key is public by design
- `await createServiceClient().from('posts').delete().eq('id', id);` in `app/api/admin/route.ts`: server code calls the service client
- `const admin = createClient(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!, process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY!);` in `app/api/users/route.ts`: route handlers run on the server
- `export const browserClient = createBrowserClient(` in `lib/supabase-browser.ts`: the anon key is meant for the browser
- `export const publishable = createBrowserClient(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!, process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!);` in `lib/supabase-browser.ts`: publishable keys are public by design
- `return createBrowserClient(url, process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY!);` in `lib/supabase.ts`: anon key in the browser
- `const admin = createClient(Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL')!, Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY')!);` in `supabase/functions/cleanup/index.ts`: Edge Functions run on the server
- `return create(import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_URL, import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY);` in `src/lib/client-factory.ts`: anon key
- `export const supabase = createClient(url, import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY);` in `src/lib/supabase.ts`: publishable key

## How to fix

Create the service role client only in server code (a route handler, Server Action, or server-only module) and use the anon or publishable key in the browser.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore data/service-role-in-client: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "data/service-role-in-client": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/data/service-role-in-client](../../../fixtures/rules/data/service-role-in-client).

<!-- docs/rules/data/firebase-open-rules.md -->

# data/firebase-open-rules

Firebase rules open to everyone.

firestore.rules or storage.rules with `allow read, write: if true`, `allow write: if true`, or the test-mode rule `if request.time < timestamp.date(...)`; database.rules.json with ".write": true.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block for public writes and for a public read of the whole Firestore database; warn for public reads of a specific path or a whole Storage bucket, public create-only rules on a specific path, writes open to any signed-in user on the whole database, a root ".read": true in database.rules.json, and everything under example and template folders. Rules under test folders are skipped.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html), [CWE-862](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/862.html), OWASP A01:2025.

## Why it matters

Firebase clients talk to the database directly with a public config, so the rules are the only access control. Open or test-mode rules let anyone read, change, or delete the data.

## Flagged

`apps/site/firestore.rules` (block):

```text
allow read: if true;
```

`apps/site/firestore.rules` (warn):

```text
allow write: if request.auth != null;
```

`examples/chat/firestore.rules` (warn):

```text
allow read, write: if true;
```

`firestore.rules` (block):

```text
allow update, delete: if true;
```

`firestore.rules` (warn):

```text
allow create: if true;
```

`firestore.rules` (block):

```text
allow read, write: if request.time < timestamp.date(2026, 10, 1);
```

`storage.rules` (warn):

```text
allow read;
```

`storage.rules` (block):

```text
allow write: if true;
```

## Not flagged

- `allow read: if resource.data.visible == true;` in `apps/site/firestore.rules`: reads limited to visible comments
- `allow update: if request.auth.uid != null && request.auth.uid == resource.data.author;` in `apps/site/firestore.rules`: author check
- `allow update: if request.auth.uid != null;` in `apps/site/firestore.rules`: signed-in writes on one path are not reported
- `allow read, write: if isOwner(userId);` in `firestore.rules`: owner check through a function
- `allow create: if request.auth != null;` in `firestore.rules`: any signed-in user may create a post on this path
- `allow read, write: if false;` in `firestore.rules`: closed
- `allow read: if request.auth != null;` in `firestore.rules`: reads for signed-in users on one path
- `&& request.resource.data.keys().hasOnly(['name', 'bio']);` in `firestore.rules`: owner check across two lines
- `allow read, write: if request.auth != null && request.auth.uid == userId;` in `storage.rules`: owner check
- `allow read, write: if true;` in `test/emulator/firestore.rules`: emulator rules under a test folder are not deployed

## How to fix

Replace the condition with a check on the signed-in user, such as `request.auth != null && request.auth.uid == userId`, and deny everything else.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore data/firebase-open-rules: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "data/firebase-open-rules": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/data/firebase-open-rules](../../../fixtures/rules/data/firebase-open-rules).

<!-- docs/rules/llm/browser-key.md -->

# llm/browser-key

LLM API key in browser code.

An LLM SDK or a direct request to an LLM API in code that runs in the browser, with a key from a public env var (VITE_, NEXT_PUBLIC_, ...) or a literal, including SDKs created with dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block for a key from a public env var or a literal in browser code; warn for dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true in server code (it has no effect there) and in browser code whose key is missing or undefined in the browser; warn in example, sample, and demo folders.
- Looks at: the project as a whole, across files.
- References: [CWE-200](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html), [CWE-522](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/522.html), [CWE-798](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html), OWASP LLM02:2025, OWASP LLM10:2025, OWASP A04:2025.

## Why it matters

Everything in the browser bundle is public: anyone who opens the site can copy the key from the JavaScript and run up usage on your account. This is the most common leak in AI-built apps that call OpenAI or Gemini straight from the browser.

## Flagged

`src/api.js` (block):

```js
apiKey: process.env.REACT_APP_OPENAI_API_KEY,
```

`app/components/Assistant.tsx` (warn):

```tsx
const anthropic = new Anthropic({ apiKey: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true });
```

`app/components/Chat.tsx` (block):

```tsx
const openai = new OpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENAI_API_KEY, dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true });
```

`lib/ai.ts` (block):

```ts
const provider = createOpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENAI_KEY });
```

`examples/browser-demo/main.ts` (warn):

```ts
const client = new OpenAI({ apiKey: import.meta.env.VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY, dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true });
```

`server/index.ts` (warn):

```ts
const legacy = new OpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY, dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true });
```

`src/api/assistant.ts` (block):

```ts
export const client = new OpenAI({ apiKey: OPENAI_API_KEY });
```

`src/api/assistant.ts` (block):

```ts
const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: ensureGeminiKey() });
```

## Not flagged

- `const openai = new OpenAI();` in `app/api/chat/route.ts`: route handlers run on the server
- `const provider = createOpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY });` in `app/api/chat/route.ts`: server-only key in a route handler
- `headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ${process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY}' },` in `app/api/chat/route.ts`: server code
- `const openai = new OpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY });` in `server/index.ts`: server code with a server-only key
- `return new OpenAI({ apiKey: userKey, dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true });` in `src/lib/openai.ts`: the user's own key
- `export const viaProxy = new OpenAI({ baseURL: '/api/openai', apiKey: 'unused', dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true });` in `src/lib/openai.ts`: the app's own proxy holds the key
- `export const local = new OpenAI({ baseURL: 'http://localhost:11434/v1', apiKey: 'ollama', dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true });` in `src/lib/openai.ts`: a local model server
- `const res = await fetch('/api/chat', { method: 'POST', headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ${token}' }, body: JSON.stringify({ prompt }) });` in `src/services/chat.ts`: the app's own API
- `const res = await fetch('https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q=${city}&appid=${import.meta.env.VITE_WEATHER_KEY}');` in `src/services/chat.ts`: not an LLM API

## How to fix

Move the model call to a server route or Server Action that reads the key from a server-only env var, and have the browser call that route.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore llm/browser-key: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "llm/browser-key": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/llm/browser-key](../../../fixtures/rules/llm/browser-key).

<!-- docs/rules/llm/output-to-sink.md -->

# llm/output-to-sink

Model output used as code, SQL, a command, or HTML.

Output of a language model call (generateText().text, result.object, choices[0].message.content, content[0].text, streamed text, useChat messages) reaching eval, new Function, child_process, raw SQL, or an HTML sink without a sanitizer or schema check.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block; warn in example or template folders. A schema parse or a sanitizer on the value clears it.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html), [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html), [CWE-89](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html), [CWE-79](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/79.html), OWASP LLM05:2025.

## Why it matters

Models follow instructions hidden in the text they read (prompt injection), so executing their output or rendering it as HTML gives whoever wrote that text control of the server or the page. OWASP LLM05 (improper output handling).

## Flagged

`app/api/report/route.ts`:

```ts
const rows = await pool.query(text);
```

`app/api/report/route.ts`:

```ts
const noted = await pool.query(`INSERT INTO notes (body) VALUES ('${object.note}')`);
```

`components/Chat.tsx`:

```tsx
<div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: marked.parse(m.content) }} />
```

`server/agent.ts`:

```ts
const result = eval(code);
```

`server/agent.ts`:

```ts
execSync(command);
```

`server/agent.ts`:

```ts
execSync(`grep -r ${args.pattern} src`);
```

`src/stream.ts`:

```ts
output.innerHTML = html;
```

## Not flagged

- `const sorted = await pool.query('SELECT * FROM invoices ORDER BY ${object.sortBy}');` in `app/api/report/route.ts`: enum field of a schema-checked object
- `const safe = await pool.query('INSERT INTO notes (body) VALUES ($1)', [text]);` in `app/api/report/route.ts`: model output passed as a parameter
- `<div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: DOMPurify.sanitize(marked.parse(m.content) as string) }} />` in `components/Chat.tsx`: sanitized
- `<p>{m.content}</p>` in `components/Chat.tsx`: JSX text is escaped
- `<div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: input }} />` in `components/Chat.tsx`: the draft the user is typing is not model output (web/xss-html-sink warns)
- `if (ALLOWED_COMMANDS.includes(command)) execSync(command);` in `server/agent.ts`: checked against an allowlist first
- `return eval(expression);` in `server/agent.ts`: not model output (reported by web/code-eval as warn)
- `const rows = await pool.query('SELECT * FROM faq WHERE topic = '${req.body.topic}' AND answer = '${text}'');` in `server/mixed.js`: request data at the same sink is reported by web/sql-injection
- `output.textContent = await result.text;` in `src/stream.ts`: textContent is not parsed as HTML

## How to fix

Treat model output as untrusted input: map it to fixed values with a schema or an allowlist, sanitize HTML with DOMPurify, and never pass it to eval, a shell, or raw SQL.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore llm/output-to-sink: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "llm/output-to-sink": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/llm/output-to-sink](../../../fixtures/rules/llm/output-to-sink).

<!-- docs/rules/llm/tool-dangerous-capability.md -->

# llm/tool-dangerous-capability

Tool passes model-chosen arguments to commands, code, SQL, files, or fetch.

A tool handler the model can call (AI SDK tool({ execute }), OpenAI Agents tool(), MCP server tools, LangChain and Mastra tools) that passes an argument chosen by the model to a shell command, eval, raw SQL, a file write or delete, or fetch, with no enum, regex, or allowlist constraint on that argument.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block for shell commands, code, raw SQL, file writes and deletes, and fetch; warn for file reads, for tools that require human approval (needsApproval), when the argument passed a schema whose constraints Ubon cannot read, and in example or template folders.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html), [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html), [CWE-89](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html), [CWE-22](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html), [CWE-918](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/918.html), OWASP LLM06:2025.

## Why it matters

Anything the model reads (a web page, an email, a file) can tell it to call the tool with arguments of the attacker's choosing, so the tool's power becomes theirs. OWASP LLM06 (excessive agency).

## Flagged

`agents/sql-tool.ts`:

```ts
const rows = await db.query(query);
```

`lib/ai/tools.ts`:

```ts
const { stdout } = await run(command);
```

`lib/ai/tools.ts`:

```ts
execute: async ({ path, content }) => fs.writeFile(path, content),
```

`lib/ai/tools.ts` (warn):

```ts
execute: async ({ path }) => fs.readFile(path, 'utf8'),
```

`lib/ai/tools.ts` (warn):

```ts
execute: async ({ path }) => fs.rm(path),
```

`lib/ai/tools.ts`:

```ts
execute: async ({ expression }) => String(eval(expression)),
```

`mastra/workflow.ts`:

```ts
await rm(context.path);
```

`mcp/server.ts`:

```ts
const { rows } = await pool.query(sql);
```

## Not flagged

- `execute: async ({ branch }) => (await run('git log ${branch} --oneline')).stdout,` in `lib/ai/tools.ts`: branch is an enum
- `return (await run(command)).stdout;` in `lib/ai/tools.ts`: checked against an allowlist
- `execute: async ({ title, content }) => fs.writeFile('notes/${randomUUID()}.md', '# ${title}\n\n${content}'),` in `lib/ai/tools.ts`: the path is generated in code; the model only writes the content
- `return sandbox.runCode(code);` in `lib/ai/tools.ts`: the code runs in a remote sandbox, not on this server
- `outputSchema: z.object({ ok: z.boolean() }),` in `mastra/workflow.ts`: z.boolean() }),
- `await rm(inputData.dir, { recursive: true });` in `mastra/workflow.ts`: a workflow step; its input comes from the workflow, not the model
- `return { ok: true };` in `mastra/workflow.ts`: true };
- `const { rows } = await pool.query('SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = '${customerId}'');` in `mcp/server.ts`: uuid format constrains the value
- `const res = await fetch('https://docs.example.com/${page}');` in `mcp/server.ts`: fixed host; the model only chooses the path
- `const { rows } = await pool.query('SELECT * FROM products WHERE name ILIKE $1', ['%${term}%']);` in `mcp/server.ts`: parameterized query

## How to fix

Constrain the argument in the input schema (z.enum() or a regex) or check it against an allowlist in the handler, and require human approval (needsApproval) for commands and file writes.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore llm/tool-dangerous-capability: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "llm/tool-dangerous-capability": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/llm/tool-dangerous-capability](../../../fixtures/rules/llm/tool-dangerous-capability).

<!-- docs/rules/llm/untrusted-system-prompt.md -->

# llm/untrusted-system-prompt

Request or fetched text in a system prompt.

Request data or the body of a network response interpolated into a system prompt: the system option of AI SDK and Anthropic calls, instructions in the OpenAI Responses and Agents APIs, Gemini systemInstruction, or a message with role system or developer.

- Default level: `warn`.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-1427](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1427.html), OWASP LLM01:2025.

## Why it matters

Models give the system prompt more authority than user messages, so text placed there by whoever sends the request, or by whoever controls a fetched page, can override the instructions that keep the model on task. OWASP LLM01 (prompt injection).

## Flagged

`app/api/chat/route.ts`:

```ts
system: `You are ${persona}. Answer briefly.`,
```

`server/summarize.ts`:

```ts
instructions: `Summarize using this page: ${page}`,
```

`server/summarize.ts`:

```ts
{ role: 'system', content: `Reply in a ${tone} tone.` },
```

`server/summarize.ts`:

```ts
system: c.req.query('system') ?? 'Be helpful.',
```

## Not flagged

- `system: SYSTEM,` in `app/api/chat/route.ts`: constant system prompt
- `messages: convertToModelMessages(messages),` in `app/api/chat/route.ts`: user messages are where user text belongs
- `input: question,` in `server/summarize.ts`: the user's question goes in the input
- `{ role: 'user', content: question },` in `server/summarize.ts`: user message
- `{ role: 'user', content: '<document>${page}</document>' },` in `server/summarize.ts`: fetched text passed as data in a user message

## How to fix

Keep the system prompt fixed in code, and pass request or fetched text in a user message, marked as data (for example inside <document> tags).

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore llm/untrusted-system-prompt: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "llm/untrusted-system-prompt": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/llm/untrusted-system-prompt](../../../fixtures/rules/llm/untrusted-system-prompt).

<!-- docs/rules/deps/undeclared-import.md -->

# deps/undeclared-import

Import of a package that package.json does not declare.

A bare import (import, export from, require, or dynamic import) of a package that the nearest package.json, the root package.json, and the workspace packages do not declare.

- Default level: `warn`.
- Levels: block in diff mode when node_modules exists and the package is not in it, because the import cannot resolve; warn when the package is installed through another dependency, when there is no node_modules, for type-only imports, and in examples, docs, and Deno code. Example, template, and docs folders without their own package.json are skipped, and so are dependencies of other workspace members when npm, Yarn (node_modules), or Bun hoists them.
- Looks at: the project as a whole, across files.
- References: [CWE-1357](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1357.html), OWASP A03:2025.

## Why it matters

An undeclared package works only by accident, because another dependency installed it, or not at all. Agents often import packages they never added, and installing such a name later without checking it is how invented package names get installed.

## Flagged

`src/app/page.tsx` (warn):

```tsx
import get from 'lodash/get';
```

`src/app/page.tsx` (warn):

```tsx
import dayjs from 'dayjs';
```

`src/app/page.tsx` (warn):

```tsx
import type { ZodSchema } from 'zod';
```

`src/app/page.tsx` (warn):

```tsx
export * from 'ramda';
```

`src/app/page.tsx` (warn):

```tsx
const ky = await import('ky');
```

`src/app/page.tsx` (warn):

```tsx
const chalk = require('chalk');
```

`supabase/functions/summarize/index.ts` (warn):

```ts
import { cors } from 'hono-cors-helper';
```

`tests/cart.test.ts` (warn):

```ts
import { setupServer } from 'msw/node';
```

## Not flagged

- `import React from 'react';` in `src/app/page.tsx`: declared in package.json
- `import Link from 'next/link';` in `src/app/page.tsx`: subpath of the declared next package
- `import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js/dist/main/index.js';` in `src/app/page.tsx`: deep import of a declared scoped package
- `import fs from 'node:fs';` in `src/app/page.tsx`: Node built-in with node:
- `import path from 'path';` in `src/app/page.tsx`: Node built-in without node:
- `import { readFile } from 'fs/promises';` in `src/app/page.tsx`: Node built-in subpath
- `import { Button } from '@/components/button';` in `src/app/page.tsx`: tsconfig path alias
- `import { money } from '~lib/money';` in `src/app/page.tsx`: tsconfig path alias with a ~ prefix
- `import Header from '@ui/header';` in `src/app/page.tsx`: bundler alias in vitest.config.ts
- `import { commit } from 'build-info';` in `src/app/page.tsx`: declared with declare module in a .d.ts file

## How to fix

Add the package with your package manager after checking it with `ubon vet <name>`, or import something the project already depends on.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore deps/undeclared-import: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "deps/undeclared-import": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/deps/undeclared-import](../../../fixtures/rules/deps/undeclared-import).

<!-- docs/rules/deps/nonexistent-package.md -->

# deps/nonexistent-package

New dependency that does not exist on the registry.

A package added to package.json that does not exist on the registry it resolves to, looked up with --online, packages.online, or `ubon vet`, or whose name is not a valid npm package name (checked offline); also an unscoped name that exists on a private registry but not on npm.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: warn for an unscoped package that exists on the private registry in .npmrc but not on registry.npmjs.org (dependency confusion). Runs only when lookups are allowed; scoped packages that .npmrc maps to another registry are looked up there or skipped, never sent to the public registry.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.
- References: [CWE-1357](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1357.html), [CWE-829](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html), OWASP A03:2025.

## Why it matters

Models invent plausible package names, and attackers register the names they invent (slopsquatting). A name nobody owns yet can be published by anyone before the next install.

## Flagged

`package.json` (block):

```json
"Bad Name": "^1.0.0",
```

`package.json` (block):

```json
"react-dom ": "^19.0.0",
```

`package.json` (block):

```json
"lodash/fp": "^4.17.21",
```

`package.json` (block):

```json
"@acme/": "^1.0.0",
```

`package.json` (block):

```json
".hidden-utils": "^1.0.0",
```

## Not flagged

- Old Name: already at the base, not added in this change
- JSONStream: uppercase letters are valid in names published before npm required lowercase
- lodash.merge and @types/node: valid names
- my-dom: an npm alias whose target, react-dom, is a valid name
- notes-ui: a workspace package, not looked up on a registry
- Git Helper: a git dependency, not installed from a registry by that name
- react-markdown-pro-renderer and @vercel/ai-sdk-helpers: new names that may not exist, but lookups are off in this run, so the rule reports them under not checked instead of guessing
- zod: a valid new name; existence needs a registry lookup
- next: a version change, not a new package

## How to fix

Remove the dependency or correct its name, and check the package with `ubon vet <name>` before adding it.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore deps/nonexistent-package: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "deps/nonexistent-package": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/deps/nonexistent-package](../../../fixtures/rules/deps/nonexistent-package).

<!-- docs/rules/deps/young-package.md -->

# deps/young-package

New dependency or version published too recently.

A package added to package.json that was first published less than packages.minAgeDays ago (default 7), or a new dependency version published less than packages.minReleaseAgeHours ago (default 48). Looked up with --online, packages.online, or `ubon vet`.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: The package install check in hooks returns "ask" instead of blocking, so a person decides. Names and scopes on packages.allow are not checked.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.
- References: [CWE-1357](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1357.html), [CWE-829](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html), OWASP A03:2025.

## Why it matters

Most malicious packages and hijacked versions are found and removed within hours or days of publication. A short cooldown keeps them out of the project while that happens.

## Not flagged

- next 15.1.2: a new version; its publish date needs a registry lookup, which is off in this run
- typescript@next: a dist-tag that usually points at a nightly build; offline it is listed under not checked
- brand-new-helper: a new package whose first publish date needs a lookup
- react: unchanged
- no finding is ever reported from a guess: without lookups the rule only says what it did not check

## How to fix

Pin a version published before the cooldown, or wait; a person can add the package to packages.allow in ubon.json.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore deps/young-package: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "deps/young-package": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/deps/young-package](../../../fixtures/rules/deps/young-package).

<!-- docs/rules/deps/typosquat.md -->

# deps/typosquat

New dependency named like a popular package.

A dependency added to package.json whose name is one edit away from a popular npm package or follows a known lookalike pattern of one: scope dropped, separators changed, a js prefix or suffix, a letter doubled or dropped, or lookalike characters such as rn for m.

- Default level: `warn`.
- Levels: The package install check in hooks returns "ask" for the same match, so a person confirms the name.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.
- References: [CWE-1357](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1357.html), OWASP A03:2025.

## Why it matters

Typosquatted packages copy a popular name with a small change and run malware when installed. Agents also misremember package names, and attackers register the misspellings they produce.

## Flagged

`package.json` (warn):

```json
"lodahs": "^4.17.21",
```

`package.json` (warn):

```json
"expresss": "^4.19.2",
```

`package.json` (warn):

```json
"react_dom": "^19.0.0",
```

`package.json` (warn):

```json
"rnongoose": "^8.0.0",
```

`package.json` (warn):

```json
"core-tracing": "^1.0.0",
```

`package.json` (warn):

```json
"axios-js": "^1.0.0",
```

`package.json` (warn):

```json
"supabase-js": "^2.45.0",
```

`package.json` (warn):

```json
"@bable/core": "^7.26.0"
```

## Not flagged

- lodash, preact, zod, vitest, @types/lodash: popular packages never match
- json-2-csv: a legitimate package that looks like json2csv, kept in the bundled lookalike list
- my-lodash: an npm alias whose real package is lodash
- zod: moved from devDependencies to dependencies, not new
- loadsh: already at the base; only its version changed
- chalkk: on packages.allow in ubon.json
- shop-utils: a workspace package
- reqeust: a git dependency, reported by deps/non-registry-source instead
- eslint-plugin-yaml: yaml and yml are two spellings, both real plugins

## How to fix

Use the name of the package you meant; if this name is intended, add it to packages.allow in ubon.json.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore deps/typosquat: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "deps/typosquat": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/deps/typosquat](../../../fixtures/rules/deps/typosquat).

<!-- docs/rules/deps/install-script.md -->

# deps/install-script

New package with an install script.

A package that is new in the lockfile, directly or through another dependency, and runs a preinstall, install, or postinstall script (hasInstallScript in package-lock.json, requiresBuild in pnpm-lock.yaml).

- Default level: `warn`.
- Levels: Skipped when the project sets ignore-scripts=true in .npmrc, and for pnpm packages that onlyBuiltDependencies leaves out or neverBuiltDependencies and ignoredBuiltDependencies list.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.
- References: [CWE-829](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html), OWASP A03:2025.

## Why it matters

Install scripts run with your permissions when the package is installed, before any of its code is imported. The Shai-Hulud worms spread through install scripts in compromised packages.

## Flagged

`package-lock.json` (warn):

```json
"resolved": "https://registry.npmjs.org/@parcel/watcher/-/watcher-2.5.0.tgz",
```

`package-lock.json` (warn):

```json
"resolved": "https://registry.npmjs.org/fsevents/-/fsevents-1.2.13.tgz",
```

`package-lock.json` (warn):

```json
"resolved": "https://registry.npmjs.org/sharp/-/sharp-0.33.5.tgz",
```

`pnpm-lock.yaml` (warn):

```yaml
/@swc/core@1.9.3:
```

`pnpm-lock.yaml` (warn):

```yaml
/sharp@0.33.5:
```

`pnpm-lock.yaml` (warn):

```yaml
/esbuild@0.25.0:
```

## Not flagged

- `ignore-scripts=true` in `.npmrc`: npm and pnpm run no install scripts in this project, so new packages with scripts are not reported
- esbuild: a new version, but esbuild already ran its install script at the base
- bcrypt: on packages.allow in ubon.json
- left-pad, chokidar-cli, react: no install script
- esbuild: a new version of a package that already built at the base
- bufferutil: listed in pnpm.neverBuiltDependencies, so pnpm does not run its script
- left-pad and ws: no requiresBuild
- `onlyBuiltDependencies:` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: pnpm builds only esbuild; the script of sharp does not run, so sharp is not reported
- left-pad: no requiresBuild

## How to fix

Check what the script does (npm view <name>@<version> scripts) before installing; if it is expected, add the package to packages.allow in ubon.json.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore deps/install-script: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "deps/install-script": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/deps/install-script](../../../fixtures/rules/deps/install-script).

<!-- docs/rules/deps/non-registry-source.md -->

# deps/non-registry-source

New dependency from outside the registry.

A dependency added in this change that comes from a git repository (git+, github:), a tarball URL, or a file: path outside the repository, or a new lockfile entry downloaded from a host that is not a configured registry.

- Default level: `warn`.
- Levels: workspace:, catalog:, link:, and file: paths inside the repository are fine. Hosts from .npmrc, .yarnrc.yml, and .yarnrc count as configured registries.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.
- References: [CWE-829](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html), [CWE-494](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/494.html), OWASP A03:2025.

## Why it matters

These sources skip the registry and its checks: there is no immutable version, no publish date, and no malicious-package record to look up, and a branch or URL can serve different code tomorrow. A changed resolved URL in a lockfile is also how lockfile injection works.

## Flagged

`package-lock.json` (warn):

```json
"resolved": "https://registry.example-mirror.net/fancy-log/-/fancy-log-2.0.0.tgz",
```

`package-lock.json` (warn):

```json
"resolved": "git+ssh://git@github.com/someone/color-support.git#3333333333333333333333333333333333333333",
```

`package-lock.json` (warn):

```json
"resolved": "https://downloads.example.com/tarball-dep-1.0.0.tgz",
```

`package.json` (warn):

```json
"left-pad": "git+https://github.com/someone/left-pad.git",
```

`package.json` (warn):

```json
"tiny-lib": "someone/tiny-lib#main",
```

`package.json` (warn):

```json
"vendored": "https://example.com/vendored-1.0.0.tgz",
```

`package.json` (warn):

```json
"shared-config": "file:../../shared-config",
```

`package.json` (warn):

```json
"gen": "exec:./scripts/build-gen.js"
```

## Not flagged

- `@acme:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com` in `.npmrc`: the @acme scope comes from GitHub Packages, so its tarball URLs there are fine
- @acme/ui: downloaded from npm.pkg.github.com, the registry .npmrc sets for @acme
- cli-helper: already a git dependency at the base; only the commit changed
- chalk and react: registry.npmjs.org
- mirror-pkg: registry.yarnpkg.com serves the public npm registry
- internal-lib: already a git dependency at the base; only the ref changed
- local-ui and @web/lib: file: paths inside the repository
- design and zod: workspace: and catalog: protocols
- linked: link: to a folder inside the repository
- my-react: an npm alias, installed from the registry

## How to fix

Install the package from the registry, or pin it to a full commit hash or an integrity-checked tarball and review the code.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore deps/non-registry-source: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "deps/non-registry-source": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/deps/non-registry-source](../../../fixtures/rules/deps/non-registry-source).

<!-- docs/rules/deps/known-malicious.md -->

# deps/known-malicious

New package with a malicious-package record.

A package or version added in this change, directly or through the lockfile, that has an OpenSSF malicious-package record in OSV (IDs that start with MAL-, looked up with --online, packages.online, or `ubon vet`), or that npm replaced with its 0.0.1-security placeholder (checked offline too).

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: OSV lookups run only when lookups are allowed, and only packages from the public npm registry are sent, by name and version.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.
- References: [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html), [CWE-829](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html), OWASP A03:2025.

## Why it matters

These records are confirmed by people: the package or version ran malware, usually when installed. Installing it again, even to test, runs it again.

## Flagged

`bun.lock` (block):

```text
"commanderr": ["commanderr@0.0.1-security", "", {}, "sha512-commanderr"],
```

`package.json` (block):

```json
"discordi.js": "0.0.1-security",
```

`package.json` (block):

```json
"noblox.js-proxy": "0.0.1-security"
```

`package-lock.json` (block):

```json
"resolved": "https://registry.npmjs.org/ua-parserr/-/ua-parserr-0.0.1-security.tgz",
```

`pnpm-lock.yaml` (block):

```yaml
colorss@0.0.1-security:
```

`yarn.lock` (block):

```text
resolved "https://registry.yarnpkg.com/axioss/-/axioss-0.0.1-security.tgz#0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567"
```

## Not flagged

- commander: already at the base
- prompt-kit 3.0.0: an ordinary version
- the project's own version field is 0.0.1-security; it is not a dependency
- left-pad 0.0.1 and security-headers ^0.0.1: ordinary versions
- old-helper: the placeholder was already in the lockfile at the base
- discordi.js and noblox.js-proxy in package-lock.json: reported once, on their package.json lines
- debug 4.4.2 and chalk 5.6.1: versions whose malicious-package records only OSV can confirm; offline they are listed under not checked
- is-arrayish: a new package; offline there is nothing to look up
- chalk and table-formatter: ordinary versions
- the snapshots section repeats colorss; it is reported once, where the package is defined

## How to fix

Remove the package, and if it was installed, treat the machine and the credentials it holds as exposed.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore deps/known-malicious: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "deps/known-malicious": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/deps/known-malicious](../../../fixtures/rules/deps/known-malicious).

<!-- docs/rules/ci/expression-injection.md -->

# ci/expression-injection

Untrusted input interpolated into a workflow script.

A `${{ }}` expression that an outsider controls (issue, pull request, and comment text, branch names, commit messages) placed directly in a `run:` script or an actions/github-script `script:`.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block when the workflow runs on events that carry secrets or a write token (issues, comments, pull_request_target, workflow_run, push, and reusable workflows), and for composite actions that such a workflow in the repository uses; warn when only fork-restricted pull_request events fill the value, for composite actions without a known caller, and for workflows outside the repository root .github/workflows. Expressions that no trigger of the workflow fills are ignored.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html), [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html), OWASP A03:2025, OWASP A05:2025, <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#understanding-the-risk-of-script-injections>.

## Why it matters

GitHub pastes the expression text into the script before it runs, so a crafted title or branch name runs as code with the workflow token and secrets. The Nx compromise of August 2025 started this way, from a pull request title in a pull_request_target workflow.

## Flagged

`.github/actions/label/action.yml` (block):

```yaml
case "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}" in
```

`.github/actions/report/action.yml` (warn):

```yaml
run: echo "## ${{ github.event.issue.title }}" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
```

`.github/workflows/pr-target.yml` (block):

```yaml
title="${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"
```

`.github/workflows/pr-title.yml` (warn):

```yaml
- run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}" | grep -Eq '^(feat|fix|chore)'
```

`.github/workflows/pr-title.yml` (warn):

```yaml
- run: echo "Branch ${{ github.head_ref }}"
```

`.github/workflows/push.yml` (block):

```yaml
-d "text=${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}"
```

`.github/workflows/push.yml` (block):

```yaml
- run: echo "${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}"
```

`.github/workflows/triage.yml` (block):

```yaml
run: echo "New issue - ${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
```

## Not flagged

- `run: echo "## $TITLE" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"` in `.github/actions/report/action.yml`: passed through env
- `gh pr comment ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} --body "Thanks! Title: $PR_TITLE"` in `.github/workflows/pr-target.yml`: number is numeric, title comes from env
- `echo "Merging into ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}"` in `.github/workflows/pr-target.yml`: the base branch is chosen by maintainers
- `- run: echo "Head ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"` in `.github/workflows/pr-title.yml`: commit SHAs are hex
- `- run: echo "Branch $GITHUB_HEAD_REF"` in `.github/workflows/pr-title.yml`: the environment variable, not the expression
- `- run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"` in `.github/workflows/push.yml`: no trigger of this workflow fills the pull request fields
- `echo "Checking issue ${{ github.event.issue.number }}"` in `.github/workflows/triage.yml`: numeric field
- `echo "$ISSUE_TITLE"` in `.github/workflows/triage.yml`: passed through env and quoted
- `if [ "${{ contains(github.event.issue.body, 'urgent') }}" = "true" ]; then` in `.github/workflows/triage.yml`: contains() returns true or false
- `const safe = context.payload.comment.body;` in `.github/workflows/triage.yml`: read from the event payload at run time

## How to fix

Pass the value through `env:` (for example `TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}`) and use "$TITLE" in the script.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```

```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "ci/expression-injection": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

<!-- docs/rules/ci/untrusted-checkout.md -->

# ci/untrusted-checkout

Pull request code run in a privileged workflow.

A pull_request_target, workflow_run, or issue_comment workflow (or a reusable workflow one of them calls) that checks out the pull request head (head.sha, head.ref, refs/pull/N/merge, workflow_run.head_sha) and then installs dependencies, builds, runs scripts, or uses a local action from it in the same job.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block; warn when the job waits for approval (a label, author_association, or actor check, a deployment environment, or a job it needs that checks permissions or membership), and for workflows outside the repository root .github/workflows. Jobs limited to same-repository or merged pull requests, and workflow_run workflows triggered only by workflows without pull request events, are skipped.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-829](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html), [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html), OWASP A03:2025, <https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/>.

## Why it matters

These workflows run with the base repository's secrets and a token that can write to it. Install scripts, build scripts, and local actions in the pull request run with that access, so anyone who opens a pull request can steal the secrets or push to the repository.

## Flagged

`.github/workflows/comment-ops.yml` (block):

```yaml
gh pr checkout ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
```

`.github/workflows/coverage.yml` (block):

```yaml
ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
```

`.github/workflows/fork-branch.yml` (block):

```yaml
repository: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name }}
```

`.github/workflows/gated.yml` (warn):

```yaml
ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
```

`.github/workflows/preview.yml` (block):

```yaml
ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/merge
```

## Not flagged

- `- run: npm ci && npm test` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: pull_request workflows run without secrets
- `- run: gh pr view ${{ github.event.issue.number }} --json title` in `.github/workflows/comment-ops.yml`: reads metadata only, checks nothing out
- `ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}` in `.github/workflows/fork-branch.yml`: a branch name alone is looked up in the base repository, where forks cannot push
- `ref: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}` in `.github/workflows/fork-branch.yml`: the head is only picked for pull_request events, which run without secrets
- `ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}` in `.github/workflows/fork-branch.yml`: only a published tool is installed and it reads the files
- `- uses: actions/checkout@v4` in `.github/workflows/preview.yml`: the base branch, which this workflow trusts
- `ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}` in `.github/workflows/preview.yml`: checked out into pr/ and only read as data
- `ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}` in `.github/workflows/preview.yml`: the job only runs for branches of this repository
- `ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}` in `.github/workflows/preview.yml`: nothing from the checkout runs
- `ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}` in `.github/workflows/release-notes.yml`: the Release workflow runs only on tag pushes

## How to fix

Build and test pull request code in a pull_request workflow without secrets, and pass results to the privileged workflow as artifacts; if you must check out the head here, do not run anything from it.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore ci/untrusted-checkout: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "ci/untrusted-checkout": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/ci/untrusted-checkout](../../../fixtures/rules/ci/untrusted-checkout).

<!-- docs/rules/ci/publish-token.md -->

# ci/publish-token

Package publishing that a stolen token or cache can hijack.

npm publish (or pnpm, yarn, changesets, semantic-release) authenticated with NODE_AUTH_TOKEN or NPM_TOKEN from a secret instead of trusted publishing; id-token: write in a workflow that pull requests trigger; a dependency cache restored in the job that publishes.

- Default level: `warn`.
- Levels: warn. Publishing to GitHub Packages or another registry set with registry-url is not reported, because those registries do not accept npm trusted publishing.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-522](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/522.html), [CWE-829](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html), OWASP A03:2025, <https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers>.

## Why it matters

A long-lived npm token in CI can be stolen by any code that runs in the job and used later from anywhere; trusted publishing issues a short-lived token per run instead. A cache restored before publishing can carry files written by another workflow run, which is how the May 2026 TanStack compromise published malware with valid provenance.

## Flagged

`.github/workflows/changesets.yml` (warn):

```yaml
cache: pnpm
```

`.github/workflows/changesets.yml` (warn):

```yaml
- uses: actions/cache@v4
```

`.github/workflows/changesets.yml` (warn):

```yaml
NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` (warn):

```yaml
id-token: write
```

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` (warn):

```yaml
echo "//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}" > ~/.npmrc
```

`.github/workflows/release.yml` (warn):

```yaml
cache: npm
```

`.github/workflows/release.yml` (warn):

```yaml
NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

## Not flagged

- `id-token: write` in `.github/workflows/changesets.yml`: push-only workflow
- `cache: pnpm` in `.github/workflows/changesets.yml`: this job does not publish
- `id-token: write` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: a test job (cloud login); forks get no OIDC token and nothing is published
- `id-token: write` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: this job runs only for tag pushes
- `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PACKAGES_TOKEN }}` in `.github/workflows/github-packages.yml`: GitHub Packages does not accept npm trusted publishing
- `id-token: write` in `.github/workflows/trusted.yml`: trusted publishing in a workflow that pull requests do not trigger
- `- run: npm publish` in `.github/workflows/trusted.yml`: trusted publishing needs no token

## How to fix

Publish with npm trusted publishing (OIDC, id-token: write) in a job that runs only on push, release, or workflow_dispatch, and restore no caches in that job.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore ci/publish-token: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "ci/publish-token": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/ci/publish-token](../../../fixtures/rules/ci/publish-token).

<!-- docs/rules/integrity/invalid-suppression.md -->

# integrity/invalid-suppression

Suppression without a valid reason.

An ubon-ignore comment that names no rule, an unknown rule, or no reason in the form `<who decided>: <evidence>`.

- Default level: `warn`.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.

## Why it matters

A suppression is a claim that a finding is wrong or accepted. Without a reason nobody can check the claim later, so Ubon ignores the comment and keeps the finding.

## How to fix

Write it as `ubon-ignore <rule>: <who decided>: <evidence>`, or remove it.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore integrity/invalid-suppression: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "integrity/invalid-suppression": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

# integrity/unused-suppression

- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.

## Why it matters

<!-- docs/rules/integrity/test-skipped.md -->

# integrity/test-skipped

Test skipped or focused in the change.

A skip or focus added to a test file: `.skip`, `.only`, `xit`, `xdescribe`, `fit`, `test.todo`, Playwright `test.fixme` and `test.skip()`, a constant `skipIf`/`runIf`, `@pytest.mark.skip`, non-strict `xfail`, Go `t.Skip()`, Rust `#[ignore]`, JUnit `@Disabled`, RSpec `xit` and `skip`.

- Default level: `block`.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.
- References: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.20270>.

## Why it matters

Coding agents skip failing tests to make a run pass instead of fixing the code (ImpossibleBench, 2025). A focused test (`.only`) silently turns off every other test in the file or run.

## Flagged

`src/slug.test.js` (block):

```js
fit('lowercases', () => { // expect-block: integrity/test-skipped
```

`e2e/checkout.spec.ts` (block):

```ts
test.fixme();
```

`e2e/checkout.spec.ts` (block):

```ts
test.describe.skip('invoices', () => {
```

`src/cart.test.ts` (block):

```ts
it.skip('adds prices', () => {
```

`src/cart.test.ts` (block):

```ts
it.only('handles an empty cart', () => {
```

`src/cart.test.ts` (block):

```ts
test.skipIf(true)('applies a coupon', () => {
```

`src/cart.test.ts` (block):

```ts
it.todo('caps discounts at 100 percent');
```

`test/api.test.js` (block):

```js
test('parses json', { skip: 'flaky on CI' }, () => {
```

## Not flagged

- `it.skip('keeps emoji', () => {` in `src/slug.test.js`: this skip existed at the base (the file is CRLF, the check compares lines without CR)
- `test.skip(browserName === 'webkit', 'The payment iframe does not load in WebKit');` in `e2e/checkout.spec.ts`: a conditional skip on a fixture value is a deliberate browser check
- `await context.clearCookies();` in `e2e/checkout.spec.ts`: context is the browser context fixture, not the Mocha alias
- `it.skip('rounds to cents', () => {` in `src/cart.test.ts`: this skip existed at the base; only the assertion below it changed
- `test.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')('uses POSIX paths', () => {` in `src/cart.test.ts`: skipIf with a real condition is a deliberate platform check
- `test.runIf(process.env.INTEGRATION === '1')('talks to the database', () => {` in `src/cart.test.ts`: runIf with a condition that can be true
- `const skip = (n: number) => n + 1;` in `src/cart.test.ts`: a helper named skip is not a test modifier
- `test('reads symlinks', { skip: process.platform === 'win32' }, () => {` in `test/api.test.js`: skip only on Windows, a condition that is false elsewhere
- `t.skip('no sandbox configured');` in `test/api.test.js`: t.skip inside a condition skips only when the sandbox is missing
- `it.skip('handles leap seconds', () => {` in `tests/utils/date.test.ts`: this skip moved with the file and existed at the base

## How to fix

Remove the skip and fix the test or the code it tests; if the test itself is wrong, tell the user instead of skipping it.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore integrity/test-skipped: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "integrity/test-skipped": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/integrity/test-skipped](../../../fixtures/rules/integrity/test-skipped).

<!-- docs/rules/integrity/test-deleted.md -->

# integrity/test-deleted

Test deleted while its code remains.

A test file deleted while the module it tests still exists, or test cases (matched by title) removed from a test file.

- Default level: `block`.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.
- References: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.20270>.

## Why it matters

Deleting a failing test makes a run pass without fixing anything, and coding agents do this under pressure to finish (ImpossibleBench, 2025). Tests removed together with the code they cover, moved to another file, or renamed are not reported.

## Flagged

`src/price.test.ts` (block):

```ts
import { expect, it } from 'vitest';
```

`pkg/calc_test.go` (block):

```text
package pkg
```

`tests/test_billing.py` (block):

```python
import pytest
```

`src/cart.test.ts` (block):

```ts
describe('cart', () => {
```

`tests/test_session.py` (block):

```python
class TestSession:
```

## Not flagged

- `describe('formatName', () => {` in `test/util/format.test.ts`: moved here from src/util/__tests__/, not deleted
- src/legacy.test.ts was deleted together with src/legacy.ts, the code it tested
- src/util/__tests__/format.test.ts moved to test/util/format.test.ts
- src/old.test.ts only held skipped tests
- src/math.test.ts only tested square(), which was removed from src/math.ts in the same change
- `it('returns the price of a single item', () => {` in `src/cart.test.ts`: "applies a discount" was removed together with applyDiscount()
- `it('returns the price of a single item', () => {` in `src/cart.test.ts`: "works for one item" was renamed; the body is the same
- `});` in `src/cart.test.ts`: "supports currencies" was already skipped at the base
- `});` in `src/cart.test.ts`: "handles negative prices" moved to cart-edge.test.ts
- `def test_sign_out(self):` in `tests/test_session.py`: test_logout was renamed to test_sign_out with the same body

## How to fix

Restore the test, or remove it together with the code it covers; if the test was wrong, tell the user instead of deleting it.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore integrity/test-deleted: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "integrity/test-deleted": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/integrity/test-deleted](../../../fixtures/rules/integrity/test-deleted).

<!-- docs/rules/integrity/type-suppression.md -->

# integrity/type-suppression

Type checking turned off in the change.

New `@ts-nocheck`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error` without a reason, `as any`, `as unknown as T`, or `: any` in a file that had none of that kind before.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block for `@ts-nocheck`; warn for `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error` without a reason, `as any`, `as unknown as T`, and `: any`. In test files only `@ts-nocheck` is reported.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.
- References: [CWE-704](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/704.html).

## Why it matters

Agents silence type errors instead of fixing them, and each escape hides the next real bug in that code. `@ts-nocheck` turns off checking for the whole file.

## Flagged

`src/api.test.ts` (block):

```ts
// @ts-nocheck
```

`src/user.ts` (warn):

```ts
export function parseUser(input: any): User {
```

`src/user.ts` (warn):

```ts
const user = input as unknown as User;
```

`src/user.ts` (warn):

```ts
return `${label}, ${(user as any).nickname}`;
```

`src/user.ts` (warn):

```ts
// @ts-expect-error
```

## Not flagged

- `const input = { id: 1, name: 'Ada' } as any;` in `src/api.test.ts`: tests cast mocks with `as any`
- `expect(() => parseUser()).toThrow();` in `src/api.test.ts`: tests pass invalid arguments on purpose
- `declare const legacyWidget: any;` in `src/globals.d.ts`: declaration files are ignored
- `const extra = JSON.parse(raw).extra as any;` in `src/legacy.ts`: this file already used `as any` at the base, so one more is not reported
- `const label: string = translate('hello.${shout}');` in `src/user.ts`: @ts-expect-error with a reason documents an expected error
- `return String(error);` in `src/user.ts`: catch (error: any) is how TypeScript types a catch clause by default
- `export const docs = 'Add // @ts-nocheck at the top of the file to turn checking off.';` in `src/user.ts`: the directive inside a string is not a comment

## How to fix

Fix the type error instead of silencing it.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore integrity/type-suppression: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "integrity/type-suppression": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/integrity/type-suppression](../../../fixtures/rules/integrity/type-suppression).

<!-- docs/rules/integrity/lint-suppression.md -->

# integrity/lint-suppression

Lint rules turned off in the change.

New lint suppressions: file-wide ones without rule names (`/* eslint-disable */`, `// biome-ignore-all lint`, `// oxlint-disable`, `# ruff: noqa`, `# flake8: noqa`, `# pylint: skip-file`) and line-level disables.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block for file-wide suppressions that name no rule; warn for suppressions that name rules, cover a range, or cover one line. In test files only the blocking kind is reported.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.

## Why it matters

Turning a linter off for a whole file hides every current and future problem in it, and agents do it to get a green run. Line-level disables are sometimes right, so they are listed for review rather than blocked.

## Flagged

`pkg/store.go` (warn):

```text
os.Remove(path + ".bak") //nolint:errcheck
```

`src/charts.js` (block):

```js
// oxlint-disable
```

`src/format.test.ts` (block):

```ts
/* eslint-disable */
```

`src/report.ts` (warn):

```ts
// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any -- legacy payload
```

`src/report.ts` (warn):

```ts
/* eslint-disable no-console */
```

`src/widgets.js` (block):

```js
// biome-ignore-all lint: the widget code is old
```

`tools/sync.py` (block):

```python
# ruff: noqa
```

`tools/sync.py` (warn):

```python
import sys  # noqa: F401
```

## Not flagged

- `export const client = { version: 1 };` in `src/generated/client.ts`: generated code (under a generated/ folder) is ignored
- `const write = console.log;` in `src/logger.ts`: this disable existed at the base; it only moved below the function
- `console.log(report([1] as any));` in `src/report.test.ts`: line-level and rule-scoped disables in tests are not reported
- `const hint = 'add /* eslint-disable */ at the top to silence everything';` in `src/report.ts`: the directive inside a string is not a comment
- `const table = [1,   2,   3];` in `src/report.ts`: biome-ignore for formatting does not turn off a check

## How to fix

Remove the suppression and fix what the linter reports.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore integrity/lint-suppression: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "integrity/lint-suppression": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

<!-- docs/rules/integrity/checks-weakened.md -->

# integrity/checks-weakened

Project checks weakened in the change.

TypeScript strictness turned off, coverage thresholds lowered, test scripts changed to swallow failures, CI steps that run tests, linters, or type checks removed or allowed to fail, and lint rules moved from error to warn or off.

- Default level: `block`.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.
- References: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.20270>.

## Why it matters

An agent that cannot make a check pass can make the check weaker instead, and the run turns green without the problem being fixed. Changes like these deserve a person's review.

## Flagged

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` (block):

```yaml
test:
```

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` (block):

```yaml
continue-on-error: true
```

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` (block):

```yaml
if: false
```

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` (block):

```yaml
- run: pytest -q || true
```

`service/pyproject.toml` (block):

```toml
fail_under = 75
```

`vitest.config.ts` (block):

```ts
coverage: {
```

`vitest.config.ts` (block):

```ts
lines: 70,
```

`package.json` (block):

```json
"lines": 60,
```

## Not flagged

- `- run: go vet ./...` in `.github/workflows/backend.yml`: go.yml was deleted, and its checks moved to this workflow
- `- name: Unit tests` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: new flags on the same test command are not a removal
- `- name: Bundle size report` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: a new optional job that is allowed to fail did not exist before
- `functions: 90,` in `vitest.config.ts`: raising a threshold is never reported
- `statements: 90,` in `vitest.config.ts`: statements unchanged
- package.json: the global branches threshold was raised from 70 to 75
- package.json: the per-folder threshold for ./src/payments/ is unchanged
- packages/lib/.nycrc: adding a reporter does not weaken anything
- `'no-unused-vars': 'off',` in `eslint.config.js`: a rule that was only a warning turned off is not a weakened check
- `'no-debugger': 'error',` in `eslint.config.js`: a new rule at error raises strictness

## How to fix

Restore the check and fix what it reports; if the change is intended, ask the user to confirm it.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore integrity/checks-weakened: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "integrity/checks-weakened": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

<!-- docs/rules/integrity/new-suppression.md -->

# integrity/new-suppression

Suppression added in the change.

A new `ubon-ignore` comment or a new entry in `.ubon/baseline.json`. Every one is listed with the rule it suppresses and the reason given.

- Default level: `warn`.
- Levels: warn by default; block when ubon.json sets `"suppressions": { "agent": "human-only" }` and the check runs for an agent session.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.

## Why it matters

A suppression turns a finding off on the word of whoever wrote it. Listing each new one keeps a suppression written by an agent visible to the person who reviews the change.

## Flagged

`.ubon/baseline.json` (warn):

```json
{ "rule": "hygiene/placeholder", "file": "src/api.ts", "fingerprint": "7d1e2c3b4a596877" },
```

`.ubon/baseline.json` (warn):

```json
{ "rule": "secret/provider-key", "file": "src/stripe.ts", "fingerprint": "a1b2c3d4e5f60718" }
```

`docs/setup.md` (warn):

```md
<!-- ubon-ignore secret/provider-key: luisfer: the key below is the public Stripe example key -->
```

`lib/payments.ts` (warn):

```ts
// ubon-ignore hygiene/placeholder: agent: the user said the sandbox URL is fine for now
```

`lib/payments.ts` (warn):

```ts
export const region = 'eu'; // ubon-ignore secret/db-url-password: agent: no password in this value
```

`scripts/deploy.sh` (warn):

```sh
# ubon-ignore secret/db-url-password: luisfer: local docker database only
```

`src/config.ts` (block):

```ts
// ubon-ignore hygiene/placeholder: agent: the preview URL is only used in development
```

`src/config.ts` (block):

```ts
// ubon-ignore secret/provider-key, hygiene/placeholder: agent: user confirmed this is a sample value
```

## Not flagged

- the secret/db-url-password entry existed at the base
- suppressions.agent is human-only, but this check is not an agent session, so new entries warn instead of blocking
- `export const testKey = 'pk_test_placeholder';` in `lib/payments.ts`: this suppression existed at the base; it only moved below charge()
- `export const other = 'your-api-key-here';` in `lib/payments.ts`: an ubon-ignore without a reason suppresses nothing (integrity/invalid-suppression reports it)
- `export const help = 'Write // ubon-ignore <rule>: <who>: <evidence> above the line.';` in `lib/payments.ts`: the syntax inside a string is not a suppression
- `export const staging = 'https://staging.example.com';` in `src/config.ts`: this suppression was approved before the session started

## How to fix

Check that the reason is true and remove the suppression if the finding is real.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore integrity/new-suppression: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "integrity/new-suppression": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/integrity/new-suppression](../../../fixtures/rules/integrity/new-suppression).

<!-- docs/rules/hygiene/elided-code.md -->

# hygiene/elided-code

Placeholder comment where code was dropped.

A comment such as `// ... existing code ...`, `// rest of the implementation`, or `/* ... */` as the only content of a body, added in the change.

- Default level: `block`.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.
- References: [CWE-1164](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1164.html).

## Why it matters

Models that rewrite a whole file sometimes write a placeholder comment instead of repeating code they did not change, and the code behind it is deleted. The file may still compile while a function body, a list of routes, or a component is gone.

## Flagged

`README.md` (block):

```md
<!-- ... rest of the file unchanged ... -->
```

`src/components/Profile.tsx` (block):

```tsx
{/* ... */}
```

`src/routes.ts` (block):

```ts
// ... existing routes ...
```

`src/routes.ts` (block):

```ts
// rest of the implementation
```

`app/worker.py` (block):

```python
# ... rest of the implementation
```

## Not flagged

- `ok: comments in fenced code blocks are documentation, not elision.` in `README.md`: comments in fenced code blocks are documentation, not elision.
- `export const routes = [` in `docs/snippets/router.ts`: code under docs/ is documentation, where placeholder comments are deliberate
- `return fn().catch((error) => {` in `src/routes.ts`: prose that starts with an ellipsis is not elision
- `export function sample() {` in `test/fixtures/rewritten.ts`: fixture files hold example input for tests
- src/cart.ts: `/* ... */` next to other code in the same body is not the only content

## How to fix

Restore the code the comment replaced from the previous version of the file, and remove the comment.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore hygiene/elided-code: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "hygiene/elided-code": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/hygiene/elided-code](../../../fixtures/rules/hygiene/elided-code).

<!-- docs/rules/hygiene/placeholder.md -->

# hygiene/placeholder

Placeholder left in runtime code.

`throw new Error('Not implemented')` and its equivalents, `TODO: implement`, lorem ipsum, `your-api-key-here` values, or example.com endpoints added to runtime code.

- Default level: `warn`.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.

## Why it matters

Agents stub out work they did not finish and report the task as done. The placeholder compiles, so it reaches users as a crash, a fake value, or a request to a domain nobody owns.

## Flagged

`app/sync.py` (warn):

```python
raise NotImplementedError("TODO")
```

`src/billing.ts` (warn):

```ts
const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/invoices', {
```

`src/billing.ts` (warn):

```ts
headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.BILLING_KEY ?? 'your-api-key-here'}` },
```

`src/billing.ts` (warn):

```ts
throw new Error('Not implemented');
```

`src/components/Hero.tsx` (warn):

```tsx
<p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.</p>
```

`src/billing.ts` (warn):

```ts
// TODO: implement
```

## Not flagged

- `raise NotImplementedError` in `app/sync.py`: a bare NotImplementedError is the usual way to mark an abstract method
- `it('calls the API', () => {` in `src/billing.test.ts`: tests use example.com endpoints and placeholder keys on purpose
- `export function refund(): void {` in `src/billing.ts`: a plain TODO about future work is fine
- `export const path = new URL('/invoices?page=2', 'https://example.com').pathname;` in `src/billing.ts`: a relative URL parsed against a dummy base
- `export const label = 'Your API key';` in `src/billing.ts`: UI copy that says "your API key" is a label, not a placeholder value
- `charge(): void {` in `src/billing.ts`: abstract base classes throw to force an override
- `<input type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />` in `src/components/Hero.tsx`: an input placeholder showing an example address
- `export const Default = { args: { title: 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet' } };` in `src/stories/Hero.stories.tsx`: stories show sample content

## How to fix

Replace the placeholder with the real implementation or value, or tell the user what is left to do.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore hygiene/placeholder: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "hygiene/placeholder": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/hygiene/placeholder](../../../fixtures/rules/hygiene/placeholder).

<!-- docs/rules/hygiene/variant-file.md -->

# hygiene/variant-file

New file named like a copy.

A file added in the change with a copy-like name (`-old`, `-new`, `_v2`, ` copy`, `.bak`, `.orig`, `-final`, a trailing `2`) next to an existing file with the base name.

- Default level: `warn`.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.

## Why it matters

Agents often write a second version of a file instead of editing the first, or keep the old one as a backup. The copy drifts, gets imported by mistake, or ships dead code.

## Flagged

`src/components/Header-new.tsx` (warn):

```tsx
export function Header() {
```

`src/lib/pricing.ts.bak` (warn):

```text
export function price(n: number): number {
```

## Not flagged

- `export const users = [{ name: 'ada' }];` in `src/api/v2/users.ts`: a versioned API folder is deliberate
- `export function Footer() {` in `src/components/Footer-new.tsx`: there is no Footer.tsx next to it, so this is not a copy
- `export const protocol = 'h2';` in `src/net/http2.ts`: http2 is a protocol name, not a copy of http.ts

## How to fix

Merge the changes into the original file and delete the copy, or give the new file a name that says what it does.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore hygiene/variant-file: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "hygiene/variant-file": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).

Fixtures: [fixtures/rules/hygiene/variant-file](../../../fixtures/rules/hygiene/variant-file).
